However, recent research exploits advanced network structures to improve performance on benchmark datasets, ignoring the vulnerability to adversarial attack. In this paper, we propose a backdoor attack method via injecting a Trojan network into victim human pose estimation networks, without retraining networks and easily to be deployed by the user. Additionally, we design an imperceptible trigger pattern for Trojan attack with semantic perturbation meaning. Experiments on the MS COCO dataset demonstrate our method achieves at least 0.2 AP score drop and maintains the performance on clean inputs against state-of-the art human pose estimation networks. Experiments have proved that the backdoor attack method for human pose estimation network is effective and harmful.

articleTitle: Semantic Feature-Driven Automatic Parameter Optimization of Apache Spark
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Big data analysis frameworks such as Spark are widely used in various scenarios, and the configuration of Spark significantly affects the execution time of the application. How to select appropriate configuration from the huge parameter space is a challenging problem currently. In the previous configuration optimization models, the semantic information of the Spark application was rarely considered. We combined the semantic information of the code to build a performance prediction model to improve the accuracy of performance prediction. For each application, parameters that have a critical impact on performance are selected to reduce the parameter space. Experimental results show that our model significantly improves the performance of Spark applications compared to Bayesian optimization and reinforcement learning-based parameter optimization models.

articleTitle: Remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries based on indirect feature and bidirectional long and short-term memory network optimized by beluga whale optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in new energy vehicles and other fields. The prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) is an essential and critical element of lithium-ion battery management systems. In this paper, we propose a framework for predicting the RUL of lithium-ion batteries using the beluga whale optimization (BWO) to optimize bidirectional long and short-term memory (BiLSTM) networks, aiming to improve the prediction accuracy of the RUL. Among them, the BWO is able to realize the automatic optimization of the network, which saves the manpower and time consumed in manual optimization while improving the accuracy effectively. To solve the problem that the capacity of lithium-ion batteries cannot be directly measured during use, indirect feature is used as a predictive feature. Firstly, several health indicators (HIs) are extracted during the battery usage. Afterwards, according to the Pearson's correlation coefficient between the HIs and the capacity, the HIs with the highest correlation are selected as the prediction feature, which ensures the reliability of indirect prediction. In this study, we conducted experiments using publicly available datasets and our own experimental datasets to verify the generalizability and robustness of the proposed method. The proposed method can realize the accurate prediction of the remaining service life of lithium-ion batteries online, which has practical application value.

Author Keywords: bidirectional long and short-term memory networks

articleTitle: Multi-scale target detection for airfield visual navigation of taxiing aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In the context of visual navigation-based civil aircraft assistance systems, the scene target scales captured by onboard cameras exhibit significant variations, and the computational power of airborne platforms is limited. To promptly and accurately identify threat targets in airborne scenic images, a lightweight multi-scale object detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv5s is proposed. Firstly, on the foundation of the Weighted Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BIFPN), a Coordinate Attention (CA) mechanism is integrated to design the CA-BIFPN feature fusion network. This enhances feature representation for small targets and improves the model's learning capability for multi-scale targets. Secondly, a cross-level sub-network module is employed to lightweightly process the neck section, reducing the model's parameter count and thereby improving the overall network's detection speed. Experimental results on a self-constructed scene image dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a detection frame rate of 89FPS, an increase of 5fps. The average precision mean (mAP) on the test set is 70.6%, a 3.4% improvement over the original YOLOv5s. The detection accuracy surpasses typical algorithms such as YOLOv6, YOLOv7, YOLOX, and Faster-RCNN.

articleTitle: Research and application of Power 5G Communication Device for Distributed Power Sources and Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In 2021, the country proposed the strategic goal of "carbon peaking and carbon neutrality". In order to actively respond to the national strategy and complete the implementation of the strategy, it was proposed to build a new type of power system with new energy as the main body. Based on 5G technology and combined with the characteristics of power grid, this paper studies the power 5G communication technology of active distribution network control, 5G MEC edge computing technology, and Beidou technology. Implemented the application of 5G+drones in line inspection. The application of 5G MEC edge computing technology in differential protection has promoted the application of 5G technology in power industry.

articleTitle: Trajectory Prediction Based on Spatio-Temporal Fusion Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The development of artificial intelligence has brought new opportunities to the field of autonomous driving trajectory prediction. Most existing research considers pairwise interaction between individual vehicle behaviors, while overlooking the impact of different information processing factors between static map information and traffic participants on predictions. This paper proposes a spatio-temporal fusion convolution trajectory prediction method based on Graph Neural Networks (STGCN). First, a novel dual-channel spatio-temporal graph mechanism is constructed to capture global map and local interaction information. Next, historical information between interacting agents is processed in the temporal dimension, introducing the temporal convolutional network to extract temporal features of historical trajectories, FusionNet is introduced to handle the spatio-temporal information. Finally, the encoder-decoder structure of GRIP++ is employed to decode the graph features and generate predicted trajectories. Experiments are conducted on the nuScenes dataset. Quantitative experiments demonstrate a significant improvement in ADE and FDE performance on the nuScenes dataset. Qualitative analysis in typical scenarios indicates that the proposed model can successfully complete prediction tasks for left turns, straight driving, and right turns.

articleTitle: Study on Railway Informatization Optimization Based on Intelligent Fusion Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This research introduces a QoS model for fundamental grid railway information services and a QoS model for composite grid railway information services to assess the efficacy of the railway information service composition within a grid environment. The study utilizes the weighted sum method to convert multi-objective optimization problems into single-objective optimization problems and devises a genetic annealing fusion algorithm for the global optimization model. Subsequently, using ticketing services as an illustration, the study validates the rationality of the QoS-based grid railway information service combination optimization model and confirms the accuracy of the genetic annealing hybrid algorithm.

articleTitle: Chinese named entity recognition based on dual-channel dilated convolution neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Chinese Named Entity Recognition (CNER) is a crucial information extraction task. However, the current mainstream models encounter issues regarding practical application in large-scale datasets or real-time scenarios. Firstly, there is a deficiency in the real-time processing of text streams due to insufficient speed and efficiency of the models. Secondly, data quality significantly affects model performance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Named Entity Recognition model (BiLSTM-DDCNN-AAT-CRF) that integrates a dual-channel dilated convolution and attention mechanism. The improved version of dilated convolutions is incorporated to enhance speed while ensuring recognition accuracy. Additionally, the IOBES tagging scheme is employed to mitigate potential model performance degradation resulting from inaccurate or inconsistent annotated data. Experimental results on the Sogou News dataset and a general dataset demonstrate a significant improvement in named entity recognition compared to existing models. Furthermore, ablation experiments validate the effectiveness of the attention mechanism and dual-channel approach proposed in this paper.

Author Keywords: bi-directional long and short term memory model

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Based Optimization Algorithm for Resource Offloading and Load Balancing in Connected Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Edge computing in Internet of vehicles accomplishes the objectives of low latency and energy consumption by offloading tasks to edge computing servers. However, how to reduce the task offloading latency and energy consumption of vehicle terminals while ensuring the priority of server computing and server load balancing is still a challenge. To solve this problem, this paper first constructs the channel model, communication model, delay model, load balancing model, and target optimization model of the Internet of Vehicles edge computing, and uses non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) communication technology. Then the paper proposes an improved Q-learning algorithm based on genetic factors (GAQ-learning algorithm) to calculate the vehicle task offloading scheme. Finally, comparative experiments were conducted between the proposed solution and various schemes. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed solution can effectively reduce the average offloading latency of users, optimize the workload between servers, and effectively reduce energy consumption, with improved performance compared to three base offloading schemes.

articleTitle: Traffic Sign Recognition Model Based on Spiking Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Traffic sign recognition is one of the key technologies for intelligent transportation and automatic driving. Most of the existing recognition methods used Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to realize the breakthrough in accuracy. But CNN has problems such as high power consumption, large computational volume and slow speed in practical applications. Spiking Neural Network (SNN) is a deep learning structure based on simulating the mechanism of processing information in biological brain, which has stronger parallel processing capability, better sparsity and real-time performance. A traffic sign recognition model is designed in this paper. A traffic sign recognition model which based on spiking convolutional neural network incorporating the spatial attention mechanism is proposed (SA-SCNN); then an optimization method of image input coding is proposed to further improve the model recognition accuracy. Experiments show that the accuracy of the model proposed in this paper is 99.56% on the GTSRB.

articleTitle: End-to-end Beamforming Design Based on Pilot in Multiuser Multi-Input-Single-Output System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning-based end-to-end system for the beamforming problem of time-division duplexing (TDD) multiuser multiple input single output (MUMISO) system under power constraints. In this paper, an end-to-end system network based on residual block embedded graph neural network (RB-GNN) is designed, which can directly parameterize the mapping from the pilots received at the base station (BS) to the beamforming matrix. RB-GNN can effectively utilize graph data structures with high-dimensional characteristics in wireless networks, and it has outstanding generalization when there is a change in user count by sharing parameters among them. The results indicate that the proposed network can obtain excellent sum-rate performance while short pilots and has good generalization ability.

articleTitle: Predicting structural dynamic responses using improved long short-term memory neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Accurately predicting the response of a structure is of great significance for health monitoring and safety assessment of structures under dynamic loads. Therefore, this paper proposes the use of an improved Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network for simulating and predicting the dynamic responses. The key point is to establish a robust LSTM network that learns dynamics from limited training data and predicts the structure's response to natural excitation. Additionally, this paper directly utilizes the structural response data as input to the neural network. Through the training of the improved LSTM, it is not necessary to use excitation data to train the model, and the response data at a specific time point in the future can be accurately predicted, which solves the problem that the full-size structure excitation cannot be measured and the structure cannot be updated based on the dynamic responses. The trained LSTM network can comprehensively learn actual structural dynamic behaviors. The proposed method bypasses complex structural modeling using finite element models, where important modeling assumptions may be ignored to cause errors. The proposed method was verified using simulated data from a four-story shear building. The results demonstrate that the trained LSTM network can accurately reproduce the responses and predict the responses which are not included in the training data.

articleTitle: Optimization of Eddy Current Loss in the Full Speed Domain of Hybrid Magnetic Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The concepts of "Carbon Peak" and "Carbon Neutral" have signaled the unstoppable trend of transforming traditional vehicles into new energy vehicles. As one of the three core components of new energy vehicles, the drive motor's performance directly affects the vehicle's performance and operation. Fractional-Slot Concentrated-Winding Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (FSCW-PMSM) has been widely favored in the new energy vehicle industry because of its many advantages. However, there are abundant magnetomotive force and armature field harmonics in the FSCW-PMSM, and the eddy current loss of the magnet steel is high at high-speed operation. Therefore, it is of great practical significance to research the magnet steel eddy current loss of FSCW-PMSM in the full speed domain, especially in the high-speed over-modulation region. In order to achieve the above objectives, a rectangular magnetic barrier hybrid magnet reluctance motor, REC-HFM, was designed. For the REC-HFM motor, a multi-objective intelligent genetic optimization algorithm is used to achieve the overall optimization of the rotor structure of the motor, taking into account the mutual influence of different parameters. The finite element analysis of the motor REC-HFM demonstrates that the motor significantly suppresses magnet eddy current losses in both the linear and over-modulation regions and exhibits good torque characteristics.

articleTitle: TESRGAN: Transformer Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of deep learning in image processing, Image Super-Resolution (ISR) has garnered extensive attention as a key technology. Recently, Transformer architectures have demonstrated immense potential across various domains, owing to their excellent ability to capture long-range dependencies. This paper explores a novel approach to incorporating Transformer architecture into the task of image super-resolution. We propose a new super-resolution model that fuses traditional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Transformer architecture, particularly in the feature extraction and image reconstruction phases. The model includes a Residual in Residual Dense Block Network (RRDBNet) for initial feature extraction, followed by a novel module named DenseResidualTransformer for further enhancement of feature representations.Our DenseResidualTransformer module combines the self-attention mechanism of Transformers with densely connected MLPs to capture global dependencies and complex textures in images. This module significantly enhances the expressiveness of feature maps through its multi-layered attention and MLP structure, while preserving the fine details of the original image. Despite the additional computational and memory overhead introduced by Transformers, our experimental results demonstrate superior image super-resolution performance on multiple standard datasets, with 31.67db of PSNR and 0.88 of SSIM, particularly in reconstructing high-frequency details and complex textures.Furthermore, we provide a detailed analysis of the application of Transformers in image super-resolution tasks, discussing the benefits and challenges it brings. The results show that incorporating Transformer architecture offers an effective way to enhance the performance of super-resolution models, especially in handling images with complex structures and textures. Our work not only demonstrates the potential of applying cutting-edge deep learning technologies to image super-resolution tasks but also provides new perspectives and directions for future research.

articleTitle: A model of assessment and intervention strategies based on SLEH
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: To address the assessment and intervention problems of multidimensional indicators, we established a light pollution risk assessment system (SLEH) to develop effective intervention strategies. Through the combined use of hierarchical analysis (AHP), entropy weighting method (EWM), and coefficient of variation method (CVM), we constructed a multidimensional SLEH model containing various indicators. This SLEH model has been applied to different types of sites and provides guidance for developing appropriate intervention strategies. In addition, we have proposed three intervention strategies and developed integer programming models and time series models. These tools have enabled us to identify the most appropriate intervention strategies and to use real data to predict the effects of interventions at different sites.

articleTitle: Research and Simulation of Satellite Communication Channel for Ship Rolling in Sea Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper realizes the satellite communication channel modeling research of ship rolling in the sea with wind and wave Since ship rolling may cause the terminal antenna to be inaccurate to the star, thus affecting the quality of satellite communication, we constructed a ship rolling model, and combined the periodic rolling angle with the satellite antenna pattern. The antenna gains variation rule of ships rolling under different ocean waves was simulated, and the channel model was generated in combination with the channel simulator. Finally, the real satellite terminal and satellite signal were used for simulation experiment, and it was found that the communication quality was very good under light waves, and it is a intermittent communication during medium waves, but the terminal could not communicate during strong waves.

articleTitle: Improved cartoon face object detector based on YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: To address the problems of low precision and inaccurate detection of cartoon character face recognition based on traditional network model, our paper proposes an improved YOLOv8 detection model based on YOLOv8n optimization. Firstly, C2f-DCN module is used to replace part of C2f, which improves the detection performance of the model; Secondly, the GAM attention module is added in the main part to strengthen the semantic information and position information in the features, which improves the feature fusion ability of the model; Finally, WIoU boundary loss function is used to replace the original loss function, which improves the bounding box regression performance of the network. The experimental results show that the detection precision of the improved model in the dataset Manga109-Face is 91%, the recall rate is 88.3%, the mAP is 93%, and the number of parameters is 4. 8*10<sup>6</sup> ; Compared with YOLOv8, the detection precision, recall and mAP are increased by 1.5%, 2.3% and 2.1%, respectively. Result shows that the proposed model improves the detection precision and has practical application value.

articleTitle: Research on the New Generation of Multi-mode Mobile Radio’s Redundant Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the rapid development of urban rail transit, higher requirements have been put forward for the real-time and reliability of wireless train command and dispatch communication. Most existing mobile radios adopt a single core processor scheme, making it difficult for the system to complete the specified functions in the event of local faults, which prolongs the fault handling time. Therefore, applying redundant technology to the control module of mobile radios has extremely important practical significance. By using the method of dual CPU redundancy switching, two CPUs verify each other, one main and one backup, ensuring information synchronization while achieving fault detection, enabling undisturbed switching function in the event of a fault. This article elaborates on the communication control module of the mobile radio for reference.

articleTitle: Meta-learning self-supervised detection based on meta-regularization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Deep learning excels in computer vision and natural language processing, seamlessly intertwining with intelligent communications. Yet, within dynamic channel landscapes, current deep learning models struggle to swiftly acclimate. Thus, a novel meta-learning-infused symbol detection framework is introduced, swiftly adjusting to diverse channel environments. Additionally, a meta-regularization approach addresses data incongruity between support and query sets. The experimental results show that the symbol error rate(SER) is reduced by 37%, which is better than other detection algorithms.

articleTitle: High-Reliability Active Miller Clamp Technique For IGBTs
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: IGBTs have been widely used in industrial applications as the mainstream power device. In a half bridge configuration, the switched-off IGBT tends to dynamically turn on during turn-on phase of the opposite IGBT, resulting in high losses and system malfunction. This paper proposes a high-reliability active Miller clamp technique for IGBTs, which builds a low impedance path between the gate and ground during the IGBT turn-off phase to prevent parasitic turn-on of the turned-off IGBT. The proposed active Miller clamp technique is designed based on the SMIC 0.18um BCD process. According to simulation results, the low level clamp peak current is 3A and the clamp reference voltage is 2V.

articleTitle: Underwater Detection using Forward-Looking Sonar Images based on Deformable Convolution YOLOv3
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Underwater target detection is crucial for the exploration and utilization of marine resources. The utilization of forward-looking sonar has become prevalent as an active sonar device for underwater perception, making target recognition based on forward-looking sonar images a subject of increasing interest. However, the complexity and variability of underwater scenes, coupled with deformations that occur during sonar imaging due to changes in the field of view pose significant challenges. This paper addresses these challenges by proposing the YOLO-DCN network, a fusion of YOLOv3 with Deformable Convolutions. These additions aim to specifically handle the deformations observed in sonar images. To enhance the robustness of underwater target detection, we employ an effective data augmentation method to address the variable nature of underwater scenes. In evaluating the performance improvement of our proposed YOLO-DCN network, we conducted experiments using the publicly available forward-looking sonar image dataset, UATD. The results reveal a notable enhancement in overall performance, with a 1.4% increase in mean Average Precision (mAP) across the ten target classes. Particularly significant is the substantial 10.2% improvement observed in the detection of irregularly shaped targets, such as the human body. This underscores the adaptability and effectiveness of our model in addressing the challenges posed by underwater sonar imaging, especially in scenarios involving complex and non-standard target shapes.

articleTitle: Mobile Network Traffic Prediction Based On Cross-Patch Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Time Series Prediction (TSP) has been effectively employed across a broad spectrum of fields since its inception and has also found success within the realm of mobile network traffic analysis. Mobile operators typically rely on the forecasts of mobile network traffic to undertake network planning and resource allocation, ultimately enhancing the quality of service provided to users. Conventional network traffic prediction methods often consider the traffic data of a single time point as a basic element and compute the dot product with other points to create an attention matrix. However, such methods are prone to the influence of random data fluctuations and usually result in extended training times. To overcome these limitations, this article introduces a novel Patch-based neural network model for predicting mobile network traffic. Traffic data is decomposed into trend and seasonal series by employing multiple sliding windows instead of one. Furthermore, the decomposed series are divided into multiple patches using different size scales, with each patch forming the base unit for computing the attention matrix, thereby reducing the impact of random data.In our experimental analysis, we conducted a comparative analysis of the predictive performance between the model proposed in this paper and the current state-of-the-art models. The results indicate that, compared to various existing Time Series Prediction (TSP) models, our proposed model exhibits superior accuracy in predicting mobile network traffic. This enhanced predictive capability highlights the potential for its effective application in mobile network traffic analysis.

articleTitle: UCA-based OAM-MIMO scheme for high-capacity wireless transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In view of the increasing scarcity of available spectrum resources and the increasing demand for wireless transmission in the future, a new wireless transmission scheme that combines orbital angular momentum (OAM) and multiple input multiple output (MIMO) is proposed. The physical layer model for a uniform circular array (UCA) based OAM-MIMO wireless transmission system is analyzed. The corresponding channel model is established by using the reference coordinate system associated with each transmitting antenna and the cumulative phase related to per OAM carrier. Basing on the channel model, the capacity and energy efficiency of the system are numerically investigated. It is found that compared with the traditional MIMO scheme, the capacity, energy efficiency and transmission reliability in the OAM-MIMO scheme have been greatly improved. The great application potential of UCA-based OAM-MIMO transmission strategy in meeting the explosive growth of wireless traffic in future is therefore revealed from a physical layer point of view.

articleTitle: Orbital Angular Momentum State Detection Method of Vortex Optical Beams under the Influence of Offset based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) is a property of light that can be used to increase the capacity of optical communications. However, due to the effect of beam offset, the performance of the detection method of orbital angular momentum may be affected. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes an orbital angular momentum state detection method based on partial convolutional neural network. The method firstly preprocesses the received optical signal, and then uses the partial convolutional neural network to extract and classify the features, so as to realize the detection of the orbital angular momentum state. Due to the characteristics of the partial convolutional neural network, the method can effectively detect vortex light in the case of incomplete reception. Through simulation experiments, we find that the channel capacity can be increased by about 25% under the influence of the offset by using the detection technology proposed in this paper. This shows that this method can not only detect the orbital angular momentum state effectively, but also eliminate the influence of beam offset to a certain extent, thus improving the capacity of optical communication.

articleTitle: Anti-Nonlinear Support Vector Machine Based Geometrically Shaping Photonic Terahertz Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low spectral efficiency and high transmission power in current photonic terahertz (THz) communication systems, a two channel signal modulation scheme based on independent sidebands (ISB) and geometric shaping (GS) is proposed, and the support vector machine (SVM) supervised learning algorithm is applied to the photonic THz communication system to achieve classification and judgment of received signal constellation points, thereby solving the problem of nonlinear effects. The simulation results show that under the transmission conditions of standard single-mode fiber (SSMF) with a carrier frequency of 90 GHz and a fiber transmission distance of 50 km, GS of the signal can achieve the best bit error rate (BER) when using a square 16QAM. At the same time, the error performance of the squared 16QAM signal with / without SVM algorithm was also measured, and the results showed that the algorithm can achieve a large received optical power (ROP) gain at a threshold of 3.8×10<sup>-3</sup>.

articleTitle: Improved Lightweight GFocal Method for Tile Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In the field of industrial production, tile defect detection is one of the key aspects of quality control. Aiming at the problems of high computational complexity and poor detection ability of small targets in industrial tile defect detection, a lightweight tile defect detection method based on GFocal is proposed. The method uses FasterNet as the backbone, which improves the coarse feature extraction ability of the model and increases the detection speed. Secondly, DFC-Involution is introduced in the multi-feature fusion part, which reduces the model parameters and improves the feature fusion ability of the model. Quality Focal Loss and Distribution Focal Loss are utilized to solve the inconsistency and inflexibility of classification and quality prediction. Finally, the BCKD module of knowledge distillation is utilized to replace the backbone with a smaller mobilenetv2, which significantly reduces the model parameters. Experimental results show that the model achieves an average accuracy (mAP) of 77.51 in tile defect detection and the parameters are reduced by 73% compared with GFocal. Compared with the industrial mainstream algorithms, the improved algorithm realizes a balance between parameters and accuracy.

articleTitle: An Extended-Range Method for Maritime Search and Rescue Radar Based on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This study proposes an extended-range method for maritime search and rescue radar based on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), aimed at expanding the detection range of traditional radar systems. A radar range-extension model combining Digital Radio Frequency Memory (DRFM) technology with UAVs is presented. This model operates by receiving radar echoes at a fixed distance using UAVs and transmitting them back to the radar receiver, thereby extending the radar’s detection range. Through theoretical analysis and simulation experiments, this study calculates the ratio of the new detection distance R<inf>new</inf> to the maximum detection range R<inf>max</inf> of conventional radars, and achieves an approximate 1.6-fold increase in range under ideal conditions. Finally, the paper demonstrates the theoretical improvements in radar detection range by UAVs, offering a more efficient and flexible technical solution for maritime search and rescue missions.

articleTitle: A Bimodal-based Algorithm for Song Sentiment Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Addressing the limitation of existing emotion classification methods for songs that only consider unimodal features from either tunes or lyrics text, and restrict classification to segments rather than the entire song, this paper proposes a novel song emotion classification algorithm based on two modalities: musical tunes and lyrics text for the entire song. Employing a two-stage self-attention method, intra-modal information within the feature vectors of lyrics and tunes is separately extracted. Subsequently, inter-modal information, fused with both modalities, is extracted. The efficacy of the proposed algorithm is validated using a self-constructed dataset and several publicly available music emotion classification datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the algorithm presented in this paper outperforms existing song emotion classification algorithms, yielding superior classification performance.

articleTitle: Research on Gear Decision Method Based on Improved Gated Recurrent Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) play a pivotal role in extracting temporal information from data, serving as an ideal neural network architecture for transforming a driver’s manual shifting experience into automated gear decisions. However, it confronts the ongoing challenge of inadequately addressing long-term sequence dependencies. Despite improvements like Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) mitigating gradient explosion, the lingering issue of gradient vanishing remains incompletely resolved. In this paper, a method is proposed based on an improved GRU to transform the driver’s manual shifting experience into automatic gear decisions. Firstly, a longitudinal motion model for the vehicle is established, and vehicle driving data are obtained. Secondly, a self-attention mechanism is introduced to enhance the GRU neural network for learning the driver’s manual shifting behavior. Finally, the gear decisions made by the improved GRU are compared with those made by the driver during manual shifting. The comparative results demonstrate that the improved GRU mitigates the issue of inaccurate gear decisions stemming from gradient vanishing. It effectively translates the manual shifting habits of drivers into precise automatic gear-shifting determinations.

articleTitle: Optical and Thermal Performance Simulation of VCSEL with Defect Type Based Photonic Crystal microcavity
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Vertical cavity surface emitting lasers (VCSELs) based on photonic crystal (PhC) microcavities can take advantage of the mode control ability to adjust the laser output mode. In this study, two types of microcavity patterns are designed. The mode field distribution, Q factor, mode characteristics and thermal effects affected by different microcavities are discussed, followed by an analysis of the Q factor and electric field distribution of microcavities with different transition hole sizes under the same pattern. The results show that the special array configuration of the air holes has a significant impact on adjusting the laser output mode, which attributed not only to the improvement of the optical field distribution but also to the improvement of heat dissipation. The side-mode suppression ratio (SMSR) of the GaAs based morning glory photonic crystal (MG-PhC) microcavity is approximately 27 dB, which is close to the single mode operation. The micro-cavity has a great electric field distribution at λ=1.078 µm, the Q factor is about 1.1×10<sup>6</sup>.

articleTitle: Dynamic Memristor based Cyclic Echo State Network for Time Series Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Compared with traditional recurrent neural networks, the training cost of echo-state network computing is lower because the neurons in the reservoir are randomly connected. We only need to train the weight of the connection between the reservoir and the output layer. Due to its high accuracy and low training cost for time series forecasting tasks, it is widely used as a time series forecasting model in many fields. It is very important to provide rich reservoir state for echo state network system, which is the key to hardware implementation. In this paper, we propose a cyclic echo state network (DC-ESN) based on dynamic memristors, which generates rich reservoir states through cyclic structure, and can predict complex time series well even with a single memristor. Compared with the traditional echo state network, the size of the reservoir is reduced and the prediction accuracy is greatly improved. Our work can provide an idea for more efficient memristor based echo state network systems in the future to cope with complex time series prediction tasks.

articleTitle: Research on Sonar Array Detection of Low Noise Targets Based on Beam Statistics
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Firstly, a linear array sonar signal model is presented. Narrowband spatial power spectrum estimation beamforming method is analyzed. Broadband beamforming process is provided. A low noise target detection and direction estimation method based on beam statistics is proposed. Finally, low signal-to-noise ratio array data is simulated using measured ship radiated noise. By comparing the statistical beamforming algorithm with conventional algorithms, the results indicate that the beamforming statistical algorithm has high accuracy in estimating the direction of low noise targets.

articleTitle: A low complexity JPEG coding system
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In the field of image compression, the traditional JPEG encoding uses a lot of multiplication operations in the discrete cosine transform and quantization. In order to reduce the computational complexity and meet the real-time requirements of the system, a low-complexity 8*8 orthogonal transformation matrix is proposed for low-bit-rate image compression, which only contains 0 and 1, without multiplication and shift operations. In addition, an approximate quantization table is designed to replace the traditional quantization table, in which addition and multiplication are not required, only shift operations are required. The results show that the image quality obtained by approximate quantization is basically the same as that of standard quantization, and the proposed coding framework can also be implemented on FPGA.

articleTitle: Raspberry Pi-Based Dual Iris Recognition System Using Coiflet Wavelet
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This study developed a dual iris recognition biometric system using the 2-D Coiflet wavelet decomposition. The system mainly consists of the Raspberry Pi 4 Model B, Raspberry Pi Camera v2 NoIR, and NIR technology. The left and right irises of the subject are captured to be processed through segmentation, normalization, and iris feature extraction using PyWavelets. With the help of the CASIA-IrisV4 database, a multi-class support vector machine (SVM) model is trained to create a system that determines genuine and impostor iris images. After a total of seventy (70) attempts, with a False Accept Rate (FAR) of 0% and False Reject Rate (FRR) of 5%, the system yielded an accuracy of 95% accuracy. The usage of Coiflet wavelet has been deemed effective for iris recognition.

articleTitle: Model Establishment and Simulation Analysis of Visible Light Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Aiming at the research status of visible light communication technology, a Lambertian model communication system based on visible light communication is designed in this paper. The power of the communication system under the Lambertian model is quantitatively studied, the power relationship of the transceiver under the direct link is constructed, and the signal-to-noise ratio of the system is theoretically analyzed. Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) spectrum analysis is performed on the receiver signal of superimposed Gaussian noise. Through Simulink simulation, the receiver waveform distortion of the communication system is low and has high communication quality.

articleTitle: Single-service Workflow Computational Offloading with Constrained Subtasks in The Multi-Edge Server Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Energy consumption is one of the main costs of running MEC (Multi-access Edge Computing) systems, and single-service workflows are composed of multiple constrained subtasks that incur a significant portion of energy consumption when offloading these subtasks to different edge nodes to complete computation. We propose an improved genetic algorithm GTGA (Game Theory Genetic Algorithm) to find an offloading scheme to minimize the energy consumption of single-service workflow computational offloading, so that each workflow in the terminal generated service workflow can achieve the goal of minimum energy consumption when calculating offloading.

articleTitle: A gas-bearing prediction model based on Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition and Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: To address the problem of weak seismic response and identification of hydrocarbon in deep reservoirs, a gas-bearing detection model based on the Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) and Deep Neural Network (DNN) is proposed. First, in order to avoid the problems of mode aliasing in the conventional empirical mode decomposition (EMD), the seismic signals are decomposed by the EEMD method. Then, a series of intrinsic mode functions (IMF) are obtained by EEMD, and the first two orders of IMF are chosen to reconstruct the seismic sub-signals. Finally, a deep neural network model is built to extract the weak fluid information straight from the reconstructed seismic data. The experimental results show that the DNN model trained on reconstructed seismic sub-signals generalizes better than the DNN model trained on raw seismic data, and can effectively indicate gas-bearing information while decreasing reliance on expert knowledge.

articleTitle: Uncertainty-Aware Robot Control via Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In recent years, model-based reinforcement learning methods have been extensively studied in the field of robot control, due to their high sampling efficiency. However, current model-based methods often don’t take into account the performance drop caused by uncertainty in robot control scenarios. To address this issue, we propose Uncertainty-Aware Model Learning (UAML). We quantify the uncertainty of the model based on model ensembles and use it to assess the accuracy of generated data. Then, we introduce a sampling-weighted mechanism to utilize the generated data. We validate the effectiveness of our approach through four robot control tasks on a high-precision simulation platform. Our method consistently outperforms state- of-the-art model-based methods.

articleTitle: Research on Gesture Recognition Based on Neural Network and Virtual Reality Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the rapid development of computer vision technology and virtual reality technology, gesture recognition has become an important way to realize human-computer interaction. In the face of increasingly complex application scenarios, background noise, self-occlusion, illumination changes and other issues will have a great impact on the accuracy of gesture recognition, which restricts the application effect of gesture recognition interactive technology. In view of this, this paper will integrate artificial neural network technology, computer vision technology and virtual reality technology, and propose a set of gesture recognition framework based on convolutional neural network, which provides a new idea for accurate and rapid gesture recognition in complex background. Practice has proved that the key points of the hand in the picture can be effectively identified by MediaPipe method, and the three-dimensional coordinates of the corresponding key points can be output. Then combined with the gesture classification model of YOLOv5 network, the input image can be predicted and the image category can be output, so that the purpose of gesture intelligent recognition can be achieved. The overall gesture recognition framework has good stability, can extract the robust features of images in complex background, improve the accuracy of gesture recognition, and effectively realize human-computer interaction in virtual environment.

articleTitle: Review on Algorithmic Models for Electric Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the rapid development of social economy, power load forecasting plays an increasingly important role in the dispatching and operation of power systems, marketization of power transactions, and energy distribution. Linear models can meet the realistic needs of forecasting in the early days, represented by differential auto-regressive integrated moving average (ARIMA). However, their insufficient accuracy in dynamic load forecasting in the context of high randomness and big data requires researchers to develop more novel models. model. Model algorithms based on machine learning and deep learning are widely used in the field of load forecasting, including temporal convolutional networks (TCN), various variants of convolutional neural networks (CNN), long short-term memory neural networks(LSTM), etc. They have stronger predictive performance and unique advantages. While the depth of the network continues to increase, the residual network is proposed to optimize the model and solve a series of thorny problems. Different models are integrated and integrated together to form a new integrated network to give full play to the advantages of each model. This paper summarizes the valuable information of the forecasting network and provides a perspective and entry point for subsequent load forecasting research work, which is helpful for researchers to explore new load forecasting methods and provides a reliable theoretical basis for power planning.

articleTitle: Multimodal Siamese Model for Breast Cancer Survival Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers, and accurate survival prediction can help doctors make appropriate treatment decisions for patients, thereby improving patient survival rates. To enhance the performance of survival prediction for breast cancer patients, a multimodal siamese model is proposed. The model utilizes a Siamese-RegNet to extract representative features, which not only considers the relationship between pathological patches but also extracts survival-related features. Moreover, The proposed model takes both pathological images and clinical data as multimodal input, which is essential to survival prediction and can improve predictive performance. The experimental results on the public dataset TCGA-BRCA and external test dataset GMUCH-BRCA demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a better concordance index (C-index) of 0.756 and 0.567, respectively.

articleTitle: Recognition of Bird Species of Gaoligong Mountain using Transfer Learning Based on VGG-16
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The study aims to build a high-quality dataset of local bird images specific to Yunnan province and use it to train and evaluate VGGNet model for bird species recognition. The research will focus on evaluating the performance of advanced VGGNet architecture, in classifying Yunnan local bird species. Firstly, established a dataset named GMBID, which consists of 5 species of bird. Secondly, we will use VGGnet, which had been pre-trained on ImageNet. In this procedure, we will use two ways to train these models: re-training and fine-tuning pre-trained model on training set. In this procedure, we focused on using transfer learning based on VGG16 model. Lastly, the testing of the trained model is performed to examine the performance.

articleTitle: Vehicle Target Detection Research Based on Enhanced YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In light of the traditional target detection algorithms with inadequate accuracy and weak robustness in modern scenarios, e.g. autonomous driving, an improved YOLOv8-based vehicle target detection algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the attention mechanism (GAM) is implemented to optimize the backbone and neck networks based on YOLOv8, improving the network's feature extraction ability. Secondly, the EIoU loss function of the Focal high-quality anchor frames is added to replace the IoU loss function, accelerating network convergence. Lastly, the Hardswish activation function replaces the original network's Sigmoid function in the global network, enhancing target detection accuracy. The experiment findings reveal that the refined algorithm enhances precision by 11.8%, recall by 1.9%, and mean average accuracy by 4.8% in comparison to the YOLOv8 algorithm on the BDD100k dataset. Alongside this, the detection speed satisfies the real-time prerequisites of autopilot, indicating the efficiency of the upgraded algorithm on the in-house dataset.

articleTitle: A Multimodal Grab Detection Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In response to the problems of low accuracy and poor real-time performance of traditional robot grasping detection methods, a multi-modal robot grasping pose detection method is proposed. Design an end-to-end grasping detection network model and train it to output the grasping pose representation parameters of the target object. This network directly predicts suitable grasping positions by fusing RGB images and depth images.The experimental results show that on the Cornell publicly captured dataset, our model accuracy is 96.6%.

articleTitle: A Graph Convolutional Network Approach for AP Selection in User-Centric Cell-Free Massive MIMO
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper studies the access point (AP) selection problem in user-centric cell-free (CF) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO). AP selection is an essential issue in user-centric CF massive MIMO, it determines the scalability and per-user spectral efficiency(SE) in the network. We propose a graph convolutional network (GCN) to address the AP selection problem. The large-scale fading coefficients are described in a graphic data structure, which is used as the input of the proposed GCN. To avoid the labeled training samples generated by a computationally complicated algorithm, an unsupervised learning framework is used for training the GCN. More specifically, the average SE of the all users is denoted as the output and the training of the GCN is to maximize the average SE by the gradient descent algorithm. The numerical results , in a specific scenario with i.i.d. Rayleigh channel model, show that the proposed GCN approach achieves a slightly higher per-user SE than the benchmark iterative algorithm.

articleTitle: Temporal Difference Attention for Action Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Temporal difference is a rough motion representation commonly employed in video action recognition frameworks. While its integration can notably enhance the recognition performance of 2D convolutional networks (2D CNNs), it may also encompass substantial regions of action-irrelevant information within the differential map. To this end, this paper proposes a streamlined Temporal Difference Attention Module (TDAM) that combines temporal difference with convolutional spatial attention to extract precise motion representation. Comparative experiments demonstrate that TDAM facilitates ResNet-50 in achieving superior results on Kinetics400 and Activity-Net datasets compared to the recent 2D CNN-based methods (74.87% and 68.71% top-1 accuracy, with only 33.1M parameters, 34.9G FLOPS, 14.6ms latency, and 68.3 FPS). Furthermore, the ablation studies on UCF101 and Activity-Net datasets reveal that the combination of bidirectional difference and convolutional spatial attention is effective and show its good generalization to convolutional architectures.

articleTitle: Characterization of Signal Transmission in Bidirectional Power Frequency Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Two-way power frequency communication technology (TWACS) is a new communication technology based on power distribution network with unique modulation and demodulation mechanism. demodulation mechanism. The article analyzes in detail the signal transmission characteristics of two-way power frequency communication for the characteristics of power distribution network in China and provides feasible suggestions for signal detection. The article analyzes in detail the characteristics of signal transmission in two-way Industrial Frequency (IF) communication for signal detection and puts forward feasible suggestions for signal detection.

articleTitle: Graph Structure-based Salient Object Detection for Point Clouds
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Salient object detection aims to detect and extract the most attractive regions relative to their surroundings, which is more challenging than traditional target detection. A point cloud is a disorganised and discrete set of points in 3D space, which inherently lacks information about the topological relationships between points. The topological relationship between points is particularly important in the task of point cloud salient object detection. Therefore, designing a model that recovers the topological relationships between points can enrich the characterisation capability of point clouds. In this paper, we explore a variety of methods for recovering topological relationships between points. They are constructing directed graphs based on coordinate space, constructing directed graphs based on feature space, constructing directed graphs based on random sampling, and constructing directed graphs based on coordinate space and features. Through analysis and visualisation, we verified that the method of constructing a directed graphs based on feature space is most suitable for recovering the topological relationship information between points. Experimental results show that this method achieves state-of-the-art performance on PCSOD public data.

articleTitle: Advancing Precision Pig Behavior Recognition through Real-Time Detection Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the growing demand for sustainable animal products, intelligent pig farming has become key to improving the efficiency of livestock agriculture. This paper employs the advanced Real-Time Detection Transformer (RTDETR) algorithm, based on Transformer technology, aiming to enhance the accuracy of pig behavior recognition. To adapt to the variable challenges of real-world environments, we have applied various data augmentation techniques to the Edinburgh Pig Behavior Video Dataset, including random cropping, horizontal flipping, RandomBrightnessContrast, and perspective transformation. By training and comparing the RTDETR with the YOLOv5 model, we observed the exceptional performance of RTDETR in complex environments, achieving a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 0.82. This research not only provides a robust algorithmic foundation for intelligent pig farming but also emphasizes the significant advantages of the Transformer-based RTDETR algorithm in improving the accuracy of pig behavior recognition in challenging environments.

articleTitle: Research on 3D Model Set Matching Based on Unsupervised Cyclic Consistency Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: To solve the problem of correspondence calculation of non-rigid 3D model set, an Unsupervised Cycle Consistency Network (UCCN) is proposed to calculate the dense correspondence of non-isometric 3D model set. First, the parameter prediction network is used to predict the deformation parameters between the two models, and then the source model is transformed into the target model through the deformation network, Finally, the cycle consistency constraint is introduced to achieve the consistency of the mapping relationship between multiple models in the model set, and the corresponding relationship between models in the model set is calculated. The experimental results show that the algorithm can effectively improve the accuracy of correspondence calculation of 3D model set. Compared with the traditional method, it realizes the mechanism of unsupervised deep learning, and does not depend on the influence of intermediate template on matching accuracy.

articleTitle: Human-Computer Interaction Data Scheduling Algorithm Based on Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Traditional scheduling algorithms have certain limitations when faced with complex tasks and dynamically changing resource environments, making it difficult to achieve efficient task allocation and resource scheduling. This paper proposes a human-computer interaction data scheduling algorithm based on artificial intelligence, and elaborates its research methods. The algorithm uses machine learning and intelligent optimization technology to learn and optimize resource allocation strategies through the analysis of historical data and real-time data, improving resource utilization and scheduling accuracy. The algorithm also has the characteristics of adaptive adjustment and decision-making optimization, and can dynamically adjust according to task characteristics and resource status to find the optimal scheduling strategy. Through the comparison and experimental evaluation of the human-computer interaction data scheduling algorithm based on artificial intelligence and the traditional scheduling algorithm, this paper obtains the research results, and the mean square error of the algorithm in this paper is kept between 0.06-0.08. In terms of resource utilization, the algorithm in this paper shows obvious advantages, which can accurately predict the resource requirements of tasks and avoid resource waste and idleness. In terms of scheduling accuracy, this algorithm can better match tasks and resources and improve task execution efficiency and response time. In terms of mean square error, the algorithm in this paper reduces prediction errors and improves system stability and performance by establishing task requirements and resource allocation models.

articleTitle: Network Traffic Anomaly Detection Based on Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Combating increasingly complex cybersecurity assaults requires an effective and efficient detection procedure, which may be achieved by integrating Machine Learning (ML) methods with well-known Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). The majority of ML-enabled IDS uses a centralized approach inside the Internet of Things (IoT), wherein IoT devices exchange data with data centers for further analysis. In recent years, a number of industries, notably healthcare and transportation systems, have shown a great deal of interest in using Federated Learning (FL) to reduce the privacy issues associated with centralized techniques. Still, research from other domains is required to determine the primary obstacles to application in real-world settings since FL-based IDS for IoT is still in its early stages of development. Specifically, this study notes that most of the existing IDSs are centralized, which may not be scalable and, more importantly, may be difficult to protect data privacy. To address this issue, this paper works as follows: utilizing CNN and BiGRU, we develop a novel IDS model that incorporates an attention method to improve the concentration on pertinent data. Additionally, we examine an FL system that comprises scattered IoT persons and federated servers, where different users from the IoT don't have to upload data but can share the model for better detection without losing privacy.

articleTitle: Adaptive Laplacian Filtering Interpolation Scaling Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In the field of video display, with the increases of resolution, the problems of transmission bandwidth, display adaptation and image display quality have gradually become prominent. To solve the above problems, we propose a new adaptive filtering interpolation scaling algorithm composed of an adaptive Laplacian filter and a bilinear interpolation scaling algorithm. The Laplacian filter alleviates the blurring effect of bilinear interpolation and enhances the image edges. Furthermore, an adaptive technology is used to enhance the effects of Laplacian filters. Bilinear interpolation was chosen for its simplicity of computation and good quality of scale. Experimental results show that compared with other methods, the average peak signal-to-noise ratio of the proposed is 0.64 dB higher than the bilinear interpolation scaling algorithm, and the calculation process is simpler.

articleTitle: Gesture recognition method based on improved YOLOv5 in complex background
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In view of the problems of low accuracy and difficult recognition of gesture detection algorithms in complex backgrounds. In this paper, a gesture detection and recognition method based on improved YOLOv5 in complex backgrounds is studied. Firstly, to ensure that the network focuses more on effective channel features in complex background images, the SE attention mechanism is introduced into both the main network and the neck network. Subsequently, without significantly increasing computational complexity, the BiFPN module is integrated into the neck network to better facilitate multi-scale feature fusion. Finally, a decoupling head is incorporated into the detection network to resolve conflicts between classification and regression during the output of variables for gesture images, significantly improving recognition accuracy. To validate the superiority of the model, a comparison was conducted with the YOLOv5s model on a custom-made dataset featuring complex backgrounds. The results demonstrate superior detection performance, especially with a 2% improvement in mAP@0.5, highlighting enhanced accuracy in gesture detection. These advancements contribute to overcoming challenges associated with gesture detection in complex backgrounds, providing a robust methodology for improving accuracy and recognition capabilities.

articleTitle: ANN-based Standard Cell Switching Waveforms Characterization Model for PVT Variations
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: VLSI circuit designs at advanced processes often necessitate addressing diverse requirements for PVT variations. In this work, we proposed an artificial neural network (ANN)-based method to characterize switching waveforms of standard cells for process-voltage-temperature (PVT) variations. Unlike traditional methods such as CCS and ECSM, our approach eliminates the prerequisite of library files for multiple PVT scenarios. Instead, every single ANN model is trained to characterize a unique standard cell with capturing its characteristics for various PVT corners. The experimental results indicate that, compared to SPICE simulations, the evaluation metrics of the switching waveforms obtained by our method have only a maximum error of 3%, an average error within 0.5%, but a minimum of 30+X of runtime improvement. Hence it will be feasible and applicable to implement such model into a commercial signoff EDA tool to reduce iterations and accelerate convergence by precisely simulating the timing, power, and EM/IR of a chip at the standard cell level.

articleTitle: Trans-CNN GAN: Self-Attention Generative Adversarial Networkd for Remote Sensing Image Super-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In recent years, deep learning based super-resolution algorithms have made breakthrough progress, especially the adversarial characteristics of Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), which is conducive to learning local details and generating more realistic images. However, most algorithms tend to overlook the large size of remote sensing images. While they focus on local features, they neglect attention to global information during the reconstruction process, resulting in the loss of information and a pronounced blurring of edge details in the reconstructed images. This article proposes a Trans-CNN GAN architecture based on self-attention mechanism, combining the advantages of GAN and Transformer. The generator adopts a CNN structure. In order to adapt to the reconstruction of large-sized remote sensing images, a discriminator containing the Transformer structure is selected. The self-attention of the Transformer is used to compensate for the convolutional generator’s lack of focus on global information, and compared with discriminator based on CNN structure to explore the impact of different discriminator structures on the generator. The method proposed in this article can effectively improve the reconstruction quality of remote sensing images. The PSNR and SSIM of the reconstructed images have been improved to 0.082 and 0.038, respectively, and the visual effect has been greatly improved.

articleTitle: DFGR: Deep Feature Graph Representation for Predicting Knee Osteoarthritis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common joint disease that severely affects the normal lives of patients. In clinical practice, the severity of KOA is evaluated by observing the X-ray images of the knee joint, which is highly dependent on the subjective experience of the doctor. In this study, we developed a novel deep CNN model that integrates structural information processing to predict KOA severity automatically. Specifically, (1) The knee joint regions of the original X-ray images are segmented using automatic detection; (2) We employed a pre-trained deep CNN models to extract deep features of key regions, and construct their corresponding graph representations; (3) A graph attention network (GAT) was designed as a fine-tuning module to build a KOA prediction model. Experiments demonstrate that our method significantly improves the performance in multiple aspects. In addition, our method demonstrates good interpretability. Codes are available at https://github.com/ddw2AIGROUP2CQUPT/DFGR

articleTitle: Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction Based on Multi-head Self-attention and Sparse Graph Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In response to the problem that existing methods cannot effectively model inter-row interactions and find it challenging to extract meaningful interaction information, a trajectory prediction method using Multi-head Self-attention (MSA) and Sparse Graph Convolution is proposed. First, we use MSA to get the spatial and temporal graphs' interaction and motion trend scores. Then, on this basis, we use the DFC mechanism and GhostNetV1 to construct the directed spatial and temporal graphs and extract pedestrian interaction and motion trend features through sparse graph convolution to obtain information on pedestrian interaction and motion trend information. Finally, the model utilizes TCN to fuse the pedestrian interaction and motion trend features and generate the predicted trajectories. The model performs better on ETH and UCY datasets, with the ADE reaching 0.35 and the FDE reaching 0.62.

articleTitle: Joint Trajectory and Power Optimization for UAV Relay Network over Time-Varying Rician Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: To enhance the reliability of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) relay communication systems, a joint optimization method for UAV relay trajectory and transmission power allocation is proposed for time-varying Rician channels. Initially, a signal reception model for the base station-UAV and UAV-user dual-hop links based on the decode-and-forward (DF) protocol is presented. A time-varying Rician channel model related to the elevation angle is established, and a first-order approximation expression for the outage probability is derived, followed by an analysis of the system’s outage performance. Subsequently, based on the criterion of minimizing outage probability, a joint optimization method for trajectory and power allocation is proposed: optimizing the transmission power allocation while fixing the UAV’s heading angle, and then optimizing the UAV’s heading angle while keeping the power allocation factor constant. Finally, simulations validate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed optimization scheme.

articleTitle: Mechanism Analysis and Simulation Implementation of Adaptive Frequency Hopping Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: As a mature and reliable anti-interference communication technology, frequency hopping (FH) communication has been widely used in the field of military communication. However, when some hopping carriers are disturbed, these disturbed carriers will continue to transmit the signal, which will affect the communication quality and even cause communication interruption. To solve the problem, an adaptive frequency hopping (AFH) communication system is proposed in this paper. The AFH consists of two core modules, namely the link quality analysis (LQA) and the frequency set configuration and update (FSCU). The former estimates the real-time channel state and locates the disturbed frequency, and the latter updates the disturbed frequency of transceiver according to the predetermined rules adaptively. Thus the communication quality is improved significantly. The proposed system is constructed in Simulink, and its efficiency and superiority were verified by vast experiments. When the bandwidth radio of the interference signal to the used one is less than 0.315, the bit error rate (BER) of AFH is close to 0 here, which outperforms the normal FH obviously.

articleTitle: Stacked LSTM-Based Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification With Blind Equalization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: As more and more wireless devices are widely connected to the Internet of Things(IoT), the authentication and identification technology of devices has become a key instrument in ensuring the security of IoT. The utilization of Radio Frequency Fingeprint (RFF)-based device identification technology can effectively achieve physical layer authentication of IoT devices. In this paper, a blind equalization (BE) based RFF extraction method is proposed, which can be performed during the process of receiving the signal without additional processing. A three-layer stacked long short-term memory (SLSTM) network is designed for employing BE-based RFF to identify different devices. The BE-SLSTM proposed in this paper achieves an identificaiton accuracy of 96.43% under a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) level of 10dB and 99.36% under 30dB, as evidenced by the experimental results from 10 radio stations.

articleTitle: A Study of Multi-Week Scheduling Scheme Based on Integer Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: As the scale of universities continues to expand, the shortage of teaching resources and the need for personalized scheduling for teachers and students has become more pressing. This article addresses the problem of university scheduling by establishing a 0-1 integer programming model, which is solved using the GUROBI solver. The model satisfies various hard constraints and generates a multi-week university scheduling plan by utilizing the relationship between university scheduling weeks. In addition, multiple soft constraints are set to produce a higher-quality class schedule. This method was applied to the scheduling of a specific semester in the computer science department of a university. Through experimental, the method was found to be highly operable and practical, and to have a significant promoting effect on the establishment and optimization of automatic university scheduling systems.

articleTitle: Causal Intervention For Robust Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have demonstrated outstanding performance in visual recognition tasks, particularly in image classification. However, the remarkable performance of DNNs is contingent upon the training and testing datasets being drawn from the same distribution (i.e., I.I.D datasets). When the testing dataset differs in distribution from the training dataset (O.O.D datasets), the model's predictive accuracy significantly decreases. In light of this, we integrate causal reasoning and propose domain-specific causal graphs to identify the reasons behind this phenomenon.
