The causal graph highlights the presence of confounding connections forming a backdoor path, which leads to the model establishing spurious correlations. Employing intervention (do) reasoning, we employ the backdoor criterion to sever the backdoor paths and, in conjunction with Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs), implement intervention reasoning. This ensures that the model learns genuine causal features for discernment without being influenced by confounding factors, thereby enhancing the model's generalization ability. We achieve outstanding performance on the out-of-distribution dataset of imagenet-9.

articleTitle: Warped Convolutional Conditional Neural Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Neural processes (NPs) constitute a family of probabilistic generative models for stochastic processes. Such models possess promising properties in terms of computational efficiency and quantification of uncertainty. However, the expression of NPs is limited as they assume that the target data obeys a Gaussian distribution, while there are many data obeying more complex distributions in real world scenarios. To address the problem of overly restrictive assumptions about data distribution, we propose Warped Convolutional Conditional Neural Process (Warped ConvCNPs). This model introduces a normalizing flow module to ensure the validity of distributional assumptions. We evaluate this model in several experiments, the results show that the proposed model has a better performance.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Noise Reduction Method for Depth Data Based on the Pulse-Coupled Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The paper proposed a noise reduction algorithm for depth data affected by noise, leveraging the Pulse-Coupled Neural Network in conjunction with an adaptive weighted median filtering approach. This method initiates the process by identifying noise points within the depth data using PCNN. Subsequently, it determines the coordinates of the filter window based on the locations of these noise points. Varied weights are then assigned in accordance with the quantity of noise data present within the filtering window. Ultimately, the weighted median filtering method is employed to process the noise data within the window, facilitating adaptive noise reduction. Experimental results illustrate that this innovative noise reduction algorithm outperforms the classic median filter algorithm across a range of noise intensities. Furthermore, it demonstrates exceptional noise reduction performance while demanding minimal computational resources.

articleTitle: An Efficient Residual-Based Neural Network for Super Resolution and High-precision Quantization Method Design
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In response to the current problems of deep layers and large model parameters in CNN for super-resolution, we propose a lightweight and efficient network model (LRSPCN) based on residuals. An efficient feature extraction module is built in model to learn effective information from row images, we induce residual connection units to achieve deep and shallow feature combination. To reduce model computational complexity, sub-pixel convolution layer is inserted in to obtain image upscale reconstruction. In our model, the amount of convolution layers and model parameters are enormously decreased. Furthermore, this paper proposes an efficient quantization method, which has the advantage of higher accuracy and lower bit-width compared to commonly used quantization methods. In our design, weight, bias and feature map are quantized uniformly to the same bit-width, which greatly compressed the storage requirements of model parameters and improved the accuracy and efficiency of hardware in edge-inference reconstruction implementation.

articleTitle: Resource-saving Design Scheme Based on Look-Up Table for Activation Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In the field of deep learning, model quantization is an important technique aimed at reducing the storage requirements and computational complexity of models to enable efficient deployment on resource-constrained devices. However, traditional model quantization methods often face high computational demands when dealing with exponential operations, especially those involving activation functions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a LUT-based method for simplifying exponential operations. Look-Up Table (LUT) is a technique that precomputes and stores function values in a table for fast querying. In this paper, LUT is employed to approximate the exponential function, significantly alleviating the computational demands of exponential operations in models. To validate the effectiveness of this method, a series of experiments were conducted. The results demonstrate that using the proposed method for activation functions improves computational speed by 22% compared to using only pseudo-quantization for activation functions. Additionally, in practical applications, this method substantially reduces the L2 error during the quantization process, further demonstrating its superiority in model quantization.

articleTitle: Point Cloud Classification Based on Local Fusion and Dense Connection Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Due to the influence of objective factors such as scene noise and hardware equipment, compared to CAD modeling point clouds, the real point clouds collected by LiDAR often have strong non-uniformity and irregularity, which leads to the low ability of traditional point cloud classification models to extract point cloud features in real scenes and poor classification robustness. To address this issue, we have added a local feature fusion module and a dense connected feature fusion method to PointMLP, thereby encoding broader point cloud information into local features. The simple stacking of multiple MLP and Mixer blocks constitutes our network model-PointMM. The shallow features of the point cloud are used as input and enter the local feature fusion module to perform feature fusion within and between point sets. Finally, by maximizing the pooling layer and selecting points with stronger semantic features as inputs to the second stage feature extraction module. This method has been tested on the ScanObjectNN dataset and shows that it can approach SOTA with a classification accuracy of 0.8%, surpassing other mainstream models.

articleTitle: Detection of Damaged Areas in Ancient Murals Based on Multi-Scale Dual Channel Attention U-Net
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: To address the issue that existing methods for detecting damage in ancient murals struggle to accurately identify damaged areas, this paper proposes a detection model based on a multi-scale dual channel attention U-Net. Firstly, a multi-scale dual channel module is designed to replace the encoder-decoder of the original U-Net, creating a network capable of detecting damaged areas of different scales in complex backgrounds. Secondly, an attention guidance module is designed to effectively merge the features of higher and lower layers. This enables the network to emphasize the prominent features of the damaged areas in murals. Additionally, this paper proposes a multi-stage loss summation strategy to enhance the performance of the network model. Experimental results on the DHMural and YNMural datasets show that this model surpasses other comparative methods in both subjective visual perception and objective evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: Sleeping position detection based on multi-domain features of ballistocardiogram
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Research shows that different sleeping positions can affect people's sleep quality. Poor sleep quality can easily lead to a variety of cardiovascular diseases. In order to better detect people's sleep conditions, this paper proposes a classification method based on ballistocardiogram (BCG). Non-contact optical fiber sensors were employed to capture BCG signals from the chest region of individuals in supine, prone, left lateral, and right lateral positions. Considering that the sleeping posture will cause the characteristic difference of the signal in time domain, frequency domain and phase, this study introduces a multi-domain feature extraction approach based on sinusoidal function fitting. This method enables the extraction of time-frequency phase features from the BCG waveform for the classification of the four sleeping postures. Experimental results demonstrate a fitting accuracy of 97% for the four-term sine function and an 83.54% accuracy for sleeping posture classification using multi-domain features.

articleTitle: Identification Method of Wind Farms Clutter Based on Statistical Distribution Characteristics of the Feature Data with Small Samples for the Airborne Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The parameter estimation, target detection, and tracking performance of the airborne radar may be affected by the wind farms. Aiming at the high dimension of the time-frequency feature data, an auto-encoder is introduced for the dimensionality reduction of time-frequency spectrum corresponding to the range resolution cell. Furthermore, in order to solve the problem of non-uniform spatial distribution of the low-dimensional time-frequency feature datasets with small samples, an identification method based on the statistical distribution characteristics and maximum likelihood is proposed. The proposed method is not limited by the distribution shape of low-dimensional feature data, and the identification performance of wind farms clutter can be improved on the condition of small samples. The evaluation indices of detection rate, accuracy rate and F1 score are established to quantitatively analyze the performance of the proposed method, and multiple sets of test scenarios are constructed to verify the stability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Local Feature Descriptor Construction Technique Based on Point Pair Features and Spatial Features and Its Quantitative Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Three-dimensional local feature descriptors are essential tools for computer vision. This study proposes a novel method to integrate geometric information based on point pair features (PPFs) and spatial features based on the polar coordinate system to process three-dimensional point cloud data. The research constructs a system of twenty-one local feature descriptors.We perform thorough experiments on four benchmark datasets and systematically examine the descriptive capacities and resilience of these descriptors.We confirm the superior performance of the twenty-one feature descriptors. The experimental results show significant differences in the performance of the descriptors based on the three geometric features. We highlight the outstanding robustness of descriptors with complex spatial and geometric features in low-quality scenarios. We propose three descriptors, namely f<inf>r</inf>(α<inf>1</inf>α<inf>2</inf>α<inf>3</inf>), f<inf>r</inf>(α<inf>1</inf>α<inf>3</inf>), and f<inf>r</inf>(α<inf>1</inf>α<inf>3</inf>), that outperform existing descriptors. This study provides substantial guidance and insights for the in-depth application and further improvement of three-dimensional local feature descriptors.

articleTitle: Fast Least Squares Multivariate Empirical Mode Decomposition for Plant-Wide Oscillation Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The plant-wide oscillation in process industry can lead to problems such as high scrap rate, high energy consumption, and reduced stability of machine operation. Aiming at the problem that existing decomposition methods are difficult to extract the oscillatory components efficiently and completely, this work proposes a fast least squares multivariate empirical mode decomposition (FLSMEMD). The method performs quantitative screening of the projected sequences according to the number of extreme points and local fluctuation characteristics, and then extracts the intrinsic mode functions from the resulting sequences. Finally, the output of FLSMEMD is derived by solving an overdetermined linear equation system. Experimental results on simulated signals and real industrial cases demonstrate that FLSMEMD is capable of effectively suppressing mode mixing and distortion. In addition, it overcomes the computational inefficiency of the decomposition process due to the redundancy of projection directions.

articleTitle: Alzheimer’s disease recognition method based on Transformers and Stacking Ensemble Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The self-attention mechanism has revolutionized the field of natural language processing and has shown remarkable progress in image analysis tasks such as image classification and object detection. In this article, we innovatively apply the Transformer model to the recognition of Alzheimer’s disease, and after verifying its good recognition accuracy and efficiency, we combine the Stacking method with other traditional training methods for classifying medical images. According to our research findings, the accuracy for binary classification (presence or absence of Alzheimer’s disease) reaches 98.51%, while for four-class classification, it reaches 97.81%. The model also achieves a average recall of 95.85% and an F1 score of 95.01%. In comparative experiments, we examined the impact of different bagging ratio values on the model, as well as several ensemble bagging methods. Furthermore, under the same parameter settings, our model outperforms VGG16, ResNet-50, and traditional CNN in terms of performance.

articleTitle: Deep graph temporal convolutional neural networks for short-term wind speed prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Due to the high randomness of wind speed in the natural environment, accurate wind speed prediction is of great significance for wind energy. With the tremendous potential demonstrated by deep learning techniques in various fields, researchers have applied this technology to wind speed prediction and achieved promising results. In this paper, to improve the accuracy of wind speed prediction, a novel network called Graph Temporal Convolutional Network (GTCN) is proposed, which effectively exploits historical wind speed features from both temporal and spatial dimensions. Based on wind speed data collected from 11 turbines in a wind farm, five baseline models are used to conduct comparative studies. The results demonstrate that GTCN exhibits superior performance in wind speed prediction.

articleTitle: Sequence recommendation based on sparse Transformer and filtering structure
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In recent years, attention mechanisms have received widespread attention and research, and have been applied to sequential recommendation systems. Although they have achieved excellent performance, there are still some problems. The historical behavior data of users often contains noise data, and the traditional attention-based sequential recommendation systems have a large number of parameters, which makes the models more likely to be affected by noise data, damaging the model performance and consuming a lot of computation time and memory. To solve this problem, this paper uses a Sparse Transformer with a sampling strategy and introduces filter layers with learnable parameters into the models, combining filtering algorithms from signal processing with cross attention mechanisms. In addition, time embedding and position embedding are introduced to enhance the model's ability to learn time information and relative position information in the interaction sequence. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, experiments were conducted on three public datasets and good results were achieved.

articleTitle: Tracking-Removed GRU with Denoising Autoencoder for Multivariate Time Series Imputation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: We propose the Tracking-Removed Gated Recurrent Unit (TRGRU) with Denoising Autoencoder (DAE) for handling missing values in the incomplete multivariate time series. The internal network of TRGRU is replicated into several subnetworks, each tasked with reconstructing a corresponding attribute of the multivariate time series utilizing information from other attributes, which removes the attribute’s self-tracking during the reconstruction. The output of TRGRU is the reconstruction of its input, enabling the utilization of observed values at the current time step in estimating missing values. These network groups share weights, leading to a reduction in overall network parameters. Additionally, we design an imputation unit based on DAE, which leverages historical information and the hidden features of input data to impute missing values within the input data and generate completed data for the training of TRGRU, enabling the model to be trained using incomplete datasets. Experimental results across multiple datasets have corroborated the effectiveness of TRGRU-DAE.

articleTitle: An Algorithm of Density Peak Clustering with Customized Cluster Quantity Based on Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Density peak clustering (DPC) is a widely used density-based clustering method. However, the clustering results obtained by DPC heavily depend on manually setting the cut-off distance, and DPC cannot generate a set of clusters with customized cluster quantity. An algorithm of density peak clustering with customized cluster quantity (CCQDPC) based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) is proposed. First, an evaluation factor is defined. The factor and customized cluster quantity are jointly regarded as the objective function of PSO, and the cut-off distance is the parameter to be optimized. Then, a set of constraints and optimization rules have been established. The two core constraints are as follows. The closer the number of clusters is to the customized quantity, the higher the quality of the particle. The larger the evaluation factor value, the higher the particle quality for particles with the same number of clusters. Finally, by iterating and evolving particles, the optimal cut-off distance is obtained, and the clustering results with customized cluster quantity and high evaluation are generated simultaneously. Seven common data sets are used for experiments. The findings demonstrate that the efficiency of CCQDPC is good, as it only requires a small particle swarm size and fewer iterations to obtain the expected clustering results. Compared to classical partitioning-based clustering algorithms, the CCQDPC algorithm has better clustering quality.

articleTitle: Palm vein recognition in few-shot learning via modified Siamese Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: As an emerging biometric technology, palm vein recognition shows many advantages that other methods do not have. With the continuous research in recent years, the implementation of palm vein recognition has developed from traditional methods to deep learning-based methods. However, deep learning requires huge numbers of labeled samples for training, and the palm vein datasets available for research are limited, which restricts the application of deep learning methods in palm vein recognition. This paper proposes a palm vein recognition method based on Siamese Network, which uses modified MobileNet V3 Large as the backbone network, it can achieve palm vein training and verification in few-shot learning. The method was tested on the Tongji University Palm Vein Database and the Hong Kong Polytechnic University Multispectral Palm Vein Database. The results suggest that the method is effective since it has 98.8% accuracy, 100% recall, 97.5% precision, 97.7% specificity , and 98.7% F1-score.

articleTitle: An Enhancement Method with Autoencoder for Deep Learning Based Hybrid Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper proposes a universal performance enhancement method for the existing hybrid beamforming structures based on deep learning (DL). The input of the existing DL-based hybrid beamforming (DL-BF) models only comprises the real and imaginary parts of the complex channel. The information hidden in the two parts tends to be ignored, leading to performance degradation. Based on the fact, the proposed method utilizes an autoencoder consist of the fully-connected layers to correlate the information between the real and imaginary parts of the complex channel matrix. The output feature from the intermediate layer of the autoencoder is extracted as enhancement information. This information is then concatenated with the original real and imaginary components of the complex channel matrix, creating an enhanced dataset for the existing DL-BF models to improve the performance. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed method can generally improve the spectral efficiency of the state-of-art DL-BF models.

articleTitle: Foreign Object Detection of Transmission Towers Based on Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: We present a transmission tower foreign object detection algorithm that integrates the attention mechanism. Firstly, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are employed for feature extraction at various scales from transmission tower images. Subsequently, a Transformer-based self-attention mechanism is combined to achieve global and local feature extraction. Finally, the Squeeze-and-Excitation attention mechanism is utilized to optimize the network's focus on specific regions, further enhancing its capability to recognize foreign objects. Experimental results demonstrate that compared with traditional methods, our method can automatically learn and focus on important regions in the image, automatically adjust the weights of features at different scales, and improve the detection performance of small and large scale foreign objects. It effectively detects four types of foreign objects on transmission towers, namely kites, balloons, bird nests, and debris, offering a novel approach to transmission tower safety monitoring.

articleTitle: Task Allocation Method for Unmanned Surface Vehicle Fleet
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In the process of collaborative operations between manned naval vessels and unmanned surface vehicles, the task allocation of unmanned surface vehicles plays a pivotal role, directly impacting the operational effectiveness of the combined task force comprising manned and unmanned vessels. Leveraging the contract network protocol, this research establishes an autonomous collaborative task allocation approach for unmanned surface vehicle fleet by constructing models for unmanned surface vehicle commander work efficiency, unmanned boat performance evaluation, and unmanned boat cost. This method takes into account both human command factors and unmanned surface vehicle factors, ensuring optimized overall allocation efficiency under comprehensive conditions. Simulation results demonstrate the feasibility of this approach, meeting the operational mission requirements of unmanned surface vehicle fleet effectively.

articleTitle: Optimization of Channel Resource QoS Allocation Based on 5G Slicing in the Field of Power Information Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The Electric Power 5G Network, serving as the foundational support for the stable operation of the smart grid, plays a pivotal role in enhancing the capabilities and efficiency of power grid management. As a pivotal technology within the realm of 5G, network slicing involves the logical segregation of network resources, thereby establishing multiple independent networks that effectively cater to distinct user demands for differentiated services. The deployment and orchestration process of network slicing inherently presents a resource allocation challenge. The efficacy of resource allocation algorithms significantly contributes to the enhancement of spectrum resource utilization while ensuring the fulfillment of Quality of Service (QoS) requisites for users.In order to address the resource allocation predicament between slices and to furnish superior service for operations, this paper introduces an optimization methodology for channel resource QoS allocation in the domain of electric power communication, hinging upon the paradigm of 5G slicing. This methodology conscientiously balances equity among various slices and the demands of users. Furthermore, a comparative analysis with proportionally fair and maximum signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio algorithms is conducted using simulation results. The outcomes underscore that the proposed algorithm can simultaneously preserve fairness while attaining elevated user spectrum efficiency.

articleTitle: Masked Image Modeling Based on Momentum Contrast
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Limited to the design of the pre-text task and the singularity of the decoder, the current Masked Image Modeling fails to achieve satisfactory global semantic representation in downstream tasks and to discern contextual information. To tackle above issues, we propose a masked image modeling framework based on momentum contrast. First, we introduce a multi-scale hidden layer fusion module to capture nuanced features. Then, the dense reconstruction decoder is designed to capture contextual information through reconstruction, while the global mapping decoder models global semantic information. Besides, the target branch updates the parameters and prevents model collapse by merging the momentum encoder. Furthermore, it extracts features from the remaining sections to stabilize the model. Last, contrastive loss is computed using the global features and the features obtained from the target branch. The experimental results on four benchmark datasets show that the proposed method can effectively improve the classification accuracy in fine-tuning and linear classification, demonstrating its strong generalization and representation capabilities.

articleTitle: Research on infrared video stabilization based on SLIC and path optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Aiming at the technical difficulties of infrared video stabilization due to parallax changes, an infrared video stabilization algorithm based on SLIC and path optimization is proposed in the paper, which mainly includes: preprocessing, improving the accuracy of motion estimation to get the camera paths, multi-path optimization, and motion compensation. In this paper, we perform SLIC processing on infrared video, using RANSAC algorithm as well as improved k-means algorithm to process the feature points to get accurate global motion estimation, and after that, we optimize multiple camera paths to get stable infrared video after compensation. After experimental analysis, our method achieves better results compared to some other traditional methods.

articleTitle: Welding Image Defect Detection Based on Yolov5
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Defect detection and identification in welding images is key to industrial process control and quality control. To overcome the limitations of existing welding image defect detection methods, the single-stage object detection model YOLOv5 is used to detect defects. The experimental results show that by using the augmented data set to train the object detector, and optimizing the hyperparameters of the network, can significantly improve the accuracy and precision of the object detector. Its accuracy and recall can reach 97.92% and 96.91% respectively, and its F1-score and mAP can reach 97.41% and 97.11% respectively. The experimental results prove the feasibility and effectiveness of the method in this paper. The algorithm can detect and locate welding images and has high application value in improving the production efficiency of the industrial manufacturing industry.

articleTitle: Lightweight Semantic Segmentation Network based on Feature Fusion and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: To address the issue of excessive parameter count, as well as the poor correlation among multi-scale feature maps and feature maps from different stages in the DeepLabv3+ network, a lightweight semantic segmentation network is proposed by introducing feature fusion and attention mechanisms on the basis of the DeepLabv3+ model. Firstly, the backbone network of the original DeepLabv3+ model is replaced with the optimized MobileNetv2 network to reduce model complexity. Secondly, an unconventional receptive field fusion strategy is employed to enhance the ASPP structure, thereby improving the information utilization and training efficiency of ASPP. Different dilation rates in convolutions are followed by the introduction of the CAM attention mechanism. Subsequently, the SAM attention is introduced after feature fusion, and the low-dimensional features are incorporated with the CBAM attention mechanism to focus on image edge features, thereby enhancing feature extraction accuracy. Finally, the model is trained using the focal loss function to improve segmentation accuracy. Experimental validation is conducted on the PASCAL VOC 2012 dataset, and the results indicate that the proposed approach further enhances segmentation performance while significantly reducing the model's parameter count.

articleTitle: Process Generation Method Based on Retrieval Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In response to the long-tail problem in the process generation, this paper proposes a retrieval-enhancement approach. This approach involves constructing an example library and retrieving similar process instances corresponding to the target process attributes, thereby enhancing the probability distribution of the model's output and better leveraging the existing data information. This method does not require retraining the existing model but only necessitates adjustments during prediction. We validated this approach on a dataset related to sheet metal manufacturing. When combining the three proposed retrieval methods with the original model, the results consistently outperformed the use of the original model alone. Specifically, the integration of the MKL method with the original model achieved an accuracy of 0.8638, an improvement of 1.66 percentage points over the original model. Furthermore, we demonstrated that this approach continues to outperform comparative methods in scenarios with limited samples.

articleTitle: Improving Implicit Geometry Learning with Multiscale Tri-Plane Feature Encoding
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid progress of deep learning in computer graphics, substantial efforts have been devoted to the exploration of diverse data structures for the representation of neural implicit fields. To boost the efficiency in learning and rendering the neural implicit fields, a novel tri-plane representation has been proposed to encode the neural radiance fields or geometry fields. Although appealing results are achieved by using the tri-plane feature encoding for the task of novel view synthesis, the potential for using tri-plane feature encoding to represent the intricate geometry is not well studied. To improve the current performance on using tri-plane feature encoding for implicit geometry learning, we propose a novel multiscale tri-plane feature encoding scheme to characterize features in different scales. Specifically, features from multiscale tri-planes are concatenated together to form a multiscale feature for learning the implicit geometry fields such as SDF. Quantitative and qualitative experiments are conducted to show the effectiveness of our multiscale tri-plane feature encoding scheme.

articleTitle: A Model Based on GCN and TCN for Malicious Code Detection in Power Information System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In recent years, as more and more Android mobile devices are connected to the power grid information system, accurate malicious code detection is very important to protect the information security of power grid. Existing methods for detecting Android malware primarily focus on learning features from a single structural type, neglecting the analysis of application semantics. This paper addresses the limitations of traditional detection methods, which fail to comprehensively capture feature semantics. To overcome this challenge, we propose an innovative Android malware detection model that combines Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) and Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN). Our model not only accurately extracts structural information from samples but also emphasizes the semantic analysis of malicious behavior. In our approach, we first characterize the topological relationships between multiple types of key system calls using a graph representation. The high-level structural information of nodes in the system call graph is then aggregated using a diffusion graph convolutional network, significantly improving the efficiency of feature learning. Next, we leverage a TCN network to capture the contextual semantics of opcode sequences. By assigning high weights to sequences with malicious features, we identify strong correlations within the features. Finally, we employ a decoder with Softmax function to output the prediction classification probability by fusing the structure information and context features. To validate the effectiveness of our model, we conduct experiments on real datasets. These experiment results demonstrate the model's validity to accurately detect and classify Android malware.

articleTitle: Multi-source Data Based Equilibrium Evaluation of Urban Parks Layout
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: As urbanisation continues, problems such as spatial congestion, population concentration and lack of environmental greenery are gradually coming to the fore. The existing urban parks have formed a scattered layout in the city, due to the needs of the service recipients, their distribution, and other environmental factors making it difficult to balance both supply and demand sides, and failure to bring the systematic method into quantitative analysis. This paper applies a new approach based on multi-source data to evaluate the supply and the demand of the urban parks in a 1000m grid size, with the help of AutoNavi API and the random forest algorithm. The study explores a statistical analysis-based perspective to improve the granularity and accuracy of the equilibrium evaluation of the urban park layout, and provide a guide to enhance the management efficiency of urban public spaces.

articleTitle: Research on road crack detection in complex background based on MFF-YOLO
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Road crack detection occupies a very important position in highway maintenance. With the development of deep learning, target detection has come into the public's view, facing the road crack data with irregular shape, complex pavement background and huge amount of data, seeking high precision, high efficiency and low cost target detector has become a popular research direction nowadays. In this paper, an improved MFF-YOLO model is proposed using YOLOv8 as the base model. By adding the BOTNet module to the backbone network, the pavement disease detection accuracy under complex background is improved; the idea of BIFPN is borrowed in the neck network, and the two-way cross-scale connection and weighted splicing operation are utilized to improve the reuse rate of the feature information and the detection effect on the small target disease; and the EIOU is used to replace the CIOU as the loss function of the detection frame regression in order to improve the model detection accuracy. The results show that the F1 value of the improved model proposed in this study reaches 69.4% and the mAP value reaches 73.7%, which are 1.3% and 3.3% higher than that of YOLOv8, respectively, and its detection accuracy is remarkable and able to cope with the detection of road cracks in complex backgrounds.

articleTitle: Study on Nonlinear Relationship Function Smulation of Fengyun 3D Satellite Microwave Dual-oxygen Sounding Observations
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The dual-oxygen channels of FY3D satellite provide a novel cloud detection approach. However, the inherent relationship between the brightness temperature observations of these channels is not necessarily linear. Fortunately, machine learning algorithms have demonstrated good simulation capabilities for nonlinear relationships. This paper explores the principles of Gaussian process regression (GPR), Extreme Learning Machine (ELM), and BP artificial neural network (BP-ANN). Firstly, we establish a new bright-temperature relationship function by examining the channel matching relationship between MWTS-2 temperature channels and MWHS-2 dual-oxygen channels. Subsequently, we investigate the application potential of three nonlinear intelligent algorithms. The results demonstrate that mean error of the GPR algorithm is only 25% of that of the ELM algorithm, which is equivalent to the BP-ANN algorithm. However, the RMSE error is only 2% of the BP-ANN algorithm. Therefore, GPR algorithm has particularly superior performance in simulating nonlinear brightness temperature relationship function. This study offers a new perspective for domestic satellite microwave cloud detection.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of High-Capacity Colorful QR Code with Multi-Code Combination
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Compared with the traditional QR code, the color QR code has the outstanding advantages of large information capacity, ease of implementation, multi-code integration, etc. Therefore, it has been generally valued at home and abroad, and various color QR codes have been developed. In this paper, based on the needs of multi-code integration, automatic identification, anti-counterfeiting traceability, and other functional applications, a new color QR code is designed according to the basic principle of QR code grey threshold discrimination reading. Adopts the printing CMYK four-color information loading and grey scale segmentation method, which has the outstanding advantages of multi-code composite, both plain code and hidden codes, universal decoding function, and anti-counterfeiting traceability. Through experimental tests, the color QR code can read the plain code by direct code scanning, and can further read or authorize to read 1-2 hidden codes by app or mini program, which can be used to meet the requirements of printing anti-counterfeiting labels, traceability of commodity information and other fields, and has a good value of promotion and application.

articleTitle: Rehabilitation gesture recognition based on improved Yolov5
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In order to improve the rehabilitation of patients with hand motor dysfunction, an improved yolov5 network model was proposed. After the CA attention mechanism is introduced into C3 module, the model pays more attention to the position features of gestures, so as to improve the ability of capturing important features in gestures. At the same time, BiFPN can better integrate information at different scales and enhance the global understanding of rehabilitation gestures. Finally, replacing the loss function to WIoU reduces the classification loss of the pack class, making it more stable and converging faster. In order to verify the improved method, this paper made a data set containing eight gestures, and conducted training on the public data set and the homemade data set. Compared with the original yolov5 model, the accuracy of the public data set was increased by 3.3 percentage points, and the accuracy of the homemade data set was increased by 3 percentage points, and the recall rate and mAP were also improved to varying degrees. The detection accuracy of gesture recognition network is improved effectively.

articleTitle: Neural Network Assisted Time-varying Non-sparse Underwater Acoustic Channel Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) technique has received much attention in the field of underwater acoustics because of its high spectral utilization. However, its performance is susceptible to inter-carrier interference, so the channel estimation performance of OFDM systems under strong Doppler non-sparse channels is highly susceptible. Most of the traditional deep learning methods only consider sparse underwater acoustic channels. In this paper, we propose a neural network-assisted OFDM-based receiver to solve the communication problem under strong Doppler non-sparse channels. Distinguished from other works that used channel frequency domain parameters as neural network inputs, we use the time-domain channel impact response matrix as input. In addition, we propose a new network model for channel characterization called ALDNet, which is an integration of an autoencoder, a long short-term memory network, and a deep neural network. This network model is employed to further optimize the results after conventional channel estimation methods. The results show that the ALDNet network model is able to obtain good performance improvement under strong Doppler non-sparse channels, and the obtained BER performance gain is more than 8dB compared with the traditional method.

articleTitle: Mobile Robot Path Planning Based on Improved Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: To address inefficiency and high collision rates in existing path planning algorithms for mobile robots in complex scenarios, this paper introduces a novel algorithm, TD3-KDHER, which combines Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) with an enhanced version of Hindsight Experience Replay (HER). The core innovation of TD3-KDHER is integrating Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) to utilize the experience buffer for fitting a probability density model, thereby optimizing the selection of pending experiences and new goals. This enhances the likelihood of selecting rare but high-value samples. Additionally, the algorithm incorporates adaptive action noise and action masking strategies to refine the exploration strategy of the agent. Experimental results show that TD3-KDHER outperforms both TD3 and TD3-HER across multiple metrics in various scenarios.

Author Keywords: twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient

articleTitle: Human Behavior Recognition Based on Attention Mechanism and Bottleneck Residual Dual-Path Spatiotemporal Graph Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Video surveillance systems are crucial tools for enhancing security and technological prevention levels. Behavior recognition plays a vital role in violence prevention and the identification of hazardous activities within video surveillance systems. Addressing challenges such as the impact of redundant backgrounds and multi-angle shooting environments on human behavior recognition in surveillance videos, resulting in poor data processing capabilities and low accuracy, this paper proposes a novel behavior detection algorithm named BiST-GCN-CBAM (Bottleneck Residual Dual-Path Spatiotemporal Graph Convolutional Network with Attention Mechanism). The model integrates bottleneck residual connections and the Channel-wise Attention Mechanism (CBAM) into the framework of spatiotemporal graph convolution. The proposed model enhances the representation capability of human behavior features, facilitating efficient recognition. Additionally, the integrated attention mechanism allows the network to focus on relevant information while disregarding unnecessary details, effectively addressing the challenge of distinguishing key nodes for different behaviors and improving recognition accuracy. Experimental results on the Kinetic-skeleton and NTU-RGB+D datasets demonstrate that the algorithm effectively reduces network computational complexity while enhancing performance, leading to accurate human behavior recognition.

articleTitle: An Active Learning based Latency Prediction Approach for Neural Network Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The multi-objective Neural Architecture Search (NAS) automates the process of neural network architecture design. It also evaluates and balances the accuracy and performance during the design process. The latency is used as a performance optimization object by many multi-objective NAS methods. A latency evaluation approach based on a latency prediction model can solve the efficiency problem of latency evaluation, but building a latency dataset of a certain scale for training the latency prediction model requires high computational costs. This paper uses multilayer perceptron (MLP) as the latency prediction model, takes an iterative selection of architectures to collect latency, trains the latency prediction model and proposes an active learning latency prediction model construction approach based on the performance of the latency prediction model to automatically stop collecting a large amount of latency data. It can avoid the high time cost problem. In the experiments, compared with the control group, using the active learning process to construct a latency prediction model for FPGA devices can save about 94% of the latency collection cost and achieve almost the same evaluation performance.

articleTitle: Joint Detection Method for Two-Way Automatic Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The channel environment of the power distribution network is extremely harsh, and the transmission of IF signal in the channel is affected by many interfering factors, which leads to a large degree of signal distortion. The single-stage adaptive trap is not effective in detecting the IF signal. To solve this problem, a joint algorithm of mathematical morphology and a two-stage adaptive trap is used to detect the IF signal. The simulation results show that compared with the single-stage adaptive trap, the algorithm in this paper reduces the average output voltage error by 1.57 V and improves the output signal-to-noise ratio by 10.5 dB.

articleTitle: Exploring Data-Efficient Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Fluid Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) is crucial in engineering applications such as aerospace and bioengineering, but it often require substantial computational resources. Learning-based simulation methods have the potential to accelerate the computation process but may require a large amount of data. This paper addresses the challenge of data-intensive demands in learning physics-based fluid simulation model by investigating the data efficiency of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for fluid dynamics. It quantifies the minimal data requirements for training PINNs, highlighting their potential to overcome the limitations of traditional CFD methods in resource-constrained environments. By establishing data efficiency benchmarks, our research supports the broader applicability of PINNs across various industries, including aerospace and environmental monitoring.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Analysis of a Dual Memristive Hopfield Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The human brain, as a large and highly complex nonlinear dynamical system, has a close connection with human intelligence activities. The artificial neural network based on memristors has shown excellent performance in simulating the working mechanism of the human brain. Therefore, in the HNN neural network, both hyperbolic tangent memristors and quadratic nonlinear memristors are introduced to couple with it. Using basic dynamical analysis methods, the paper discusses the dynamical behavior of the system under different coupling strengths and studies the behavior of attractor symmetry under different initial values. The experimental results show that under different memristor parameters, by observing the changes in the phase trajectory diagram, Lyapunov exponent, and bifurcation diagram of the system, it is found that it has periodic doubling bifurcation, chaos, periodic window, and double vortex attractor symmetry behavior. At the same time, it also emphasizes its full sensitivity to initial values. At the same time, its complex dynamical characteristics also provide research support for applications in data processing, image encryption, biomedical, and other fields.

articleTitle: Lidar-Assisted Visual Localization System Based on Factor Graph Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-precision localization system for improving the stability and positioning accuracy of robots in dynamic environments. The system is based on graph optimization and integrates data from multiple sensors. By fusing data from laser rangefinders, inertial measurement units, and visual tag measurements through graph optimization, the robot can achieve faster and more accurate localization with higher precision. This method addresses the challenges of failure cases where laser odometry fails to match specific environments and the issue of position drift caused by environmental factors in marker-based localization. Comparative experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Fourier Ptychographic Microscopy reconstruction method based on the self-attention mechanism of shifted convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Traditional deep learning models usually produce redundant operations during image reconstruction, leading to a waste of computational resources and limiting the performance of the model, the reconstructed images have the problems of unclear edge and incomplete local information. To address this problem, this paper introduces a Fourier Ptychographic Microscopy reconstruction combining shift convolution and spatial attention channels. Shift convolution can improve the speed of network reconstruction and reduce the waste of computational resources, while the self-attention mechanism can better capture key features in the image and retain important contextual information, thus achieving higher reconstruction accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: Emotion-Aware Talking Face Generation Based on 3DMM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Current methods for generating videos of talking face based on deep learning mainly focus on the correlation between lip movements and audio content. Although these methods have high generation quality and good audio-visual synchronization, they ignore facial expressions in talking face videos. To solve this problem, Audio to Expression Network (A2ENet), an emotional talking face video generation framework based on 3DMM, is proposed in this paper to generate talking face videos with facial expressions in an audio-driven way. Firstly, A2ENet uses two Transformer based encoders to extract audio features, and uses a cross-reconstruction emotion disentanglement method to decompose audio into potential space of content information and potential space of emotion information, and then uses a Transformer Decoder to integrate these two feature spaces. After that, the Proposed method predict the 3D expression coefficient that matches the emotion of the audio, and finally uses the renderer to generate the talking face video. By using the eye control parameters, A2ENet can realize the eye movements control of talking face. A2ENet associating the initial 3D expression coefficients with specific individuals to retain the identity information of the reference face. Experimental results show that our method can generate talking face videos with appropriate facial expressions, and achieve more accurate lip movements and better video quality.

articleTitle: Resource Management with Blockchain for Delay-Sensitive Transmission in UAV-assisted Vehicular Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In this paper, we present a blockchain based resource allocation scheme on UAV-assisted communication in vehicular network. Our design aims to minimize the system delay by coordinating the spectrum sharing and power consumption of the secondary UAVs under the tolerated interference limitation of the primary UAVs. In the main process of the blockchain application, firstly, the spectrum request of the UAVs is formulated as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem to select the channel and power value. Then, within a limited power range and time delay requirements, the resource request is broadcasted, and the voting is conducted according to the Ripple consensus mechanism. Finally, the transaction record is packaged into a new ledger and attached to the whole ledgers. Simulation results show that the proposed blockchain-based resource management scheme can improve the communication reliability, real-time character and vehicular rate.

articleTitle: A lightweight IoT terminal authentication method based on the SM algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In the distributed power network, the secure access of terminal equipment is closely related to the security of the power grid system. Usually, the terminal can achieve device access through two-way authentication with the edge-side device under the distributed architecture. Therefore, aiming at the security problem of the power network, a two-way authentication method between the edge side device and the terminal of the physical network based on the national secret encryption algorithm was designed, in which digital signature technology was used to exchange secret key information. The shared key is generated based on the Diffie-Hellman protocol. In addition, considering the problem of insufficient performance of IoT terminals, the authentication method was lightweight from the perspective of computational overhead and transmission overhead. Through theoretical verification, this method can fully resist reusing, eavesdropping, tampering, and other network attacks to achieve mutual authentication between devices.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Multi-label Classification Method for Maritime Distress Safety Information
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Maritime distress safety (MDS) text information hierarchical multi-label text classification (HMTC) involves categorizing MDS texts into a label set with a hierarchical structure. Due to the varying impact of specific keywords in MDS text information on certain labels within the hierarchical label system, an improved TF-IDF-Keyword-Filtering (TIKF) algorithm based on the traditional TF-IDF algorithm and the KABLG model are proposed to highlight these keywords. The TIKF algorithm incorporates intra-parent class correlation, inter-class correlation, and term frequency factor to calculate the weight of each feature keyword. It also utilizes a pre-trained Word2Vec model to construct new keyword vectors for keyword filtering. This reduces the influence of unimportant words, filters out specific keywords that are more important for hierarchical labels, and accelerates the model learning process. The KABLG model uses Bi-LSTM and hierarchy-GCN to respectively extract contextual information and hierarchical label representations. It designs interactions between textual features and label features, and adaptively integrates them with keyword features, resulting in improved classification performance of the model. We prove the effectiveness of the TIKF algorithm and the KABLG model on the MDS dataset.

articleTitle: Design of High Linearity DAC for impedance enhanced current source
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The current source array is the core circuit of a digital to analog converter (DAC), and its performance directly affects the performance indicators of the DAC.A new type of high linearity DAC is designed to address the two major factors that affect DAC linearity in traditional current source arrays: clock feedthrough effect in transient switches and limited output impedance. It introduces a "dummy" switch to compensate for the clock feedthrough effect and reduce the bugs in the output waveform.At the same time, the "gain boosting" technology was adapted to design an auxiliary operational amplifier, which utilizes its advantage of increasing the output impedance on the signal path,further improving the spurious free dynamic range(SFDR) of the DAC.Based on SMIC 180nm CMOS technology, post simulation verification was conducted on DAC.The results showed that under the conditions of input frequency of 1.025 MHz and sampling rate of 200 MS/s,the Differential Non-Linearity (DNL) is 0.12 LSB, the Integral Non-Linearity (INL) is 0.23 LSB, the SFDR is 80.2 dB,and the signal to noise distortion ratio (SNDR) to be 70.15 dB.

articleTitle: Research on Image Forgery Detection Based on Fusion Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The rapid proliferation of digital image forgery has exacerbated a crisis of trust in society. Consequently, image forgery detection has garnered increasing attention in computer vision field. Despite the existence of numerous algorithms for image forgery detection, the utilization of lightweight models remains significantly insufficient. Many researchers encounter challenges due to limited resources for training and deploying models. To address this issue, this paper proposed an approach composed of different lightweight models. Specifically, it comprises two key components: 1) a fusion model module that acquires diverse feature maps from various lightweight networks, enabling the fused network to attend to a broader range of information; 2) treating image forgery detection as a binary classification problem, with the fused feature map fed into a Random Forest for classification. Furthermore, we also conducted some ablation experiments to validate the superior performance of our method.

articleTitle: Simulation of Spread Spectrum Communication System Based on MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: After 1980s, the application field of spread spectrum communication has been greatly expanded,from the former military field to the commercial field. For example,in the new generation of digital honeycomb applications,that is,mobile phone communication, for example,in the field of satellite communication,direct sequence spread spectrum and frequency hopping can reduce communication interference,and in the field of global positioning applications,such as GPS and Beidou navigation system,its application field and application range are still expanding. In this paper,Matlab simulation program is used to simulate the simulation process of spread spectrum communication, the specific role of each module and the detailed parameters of the module are introduced,the theoretical basis of spread spectrum communication and the simulation of spread spectrum communication system are expounded, and the simulation program is run under the given simulation conditions and the expected simulation results are obtained. The results show that the spread spectrum communication system has strong antijamming and is of great significance to the communication system.

articleTitle: Research of an Enhanced YOLOv5-Based Algorithm for Garbage Detection in Service Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Addressing the challenge of effectively detecting service area litter through monitoring systems, this study introduces an improved YOLOv5 object detection algorithm. To begin, the backbone feature extraction network of YOLOv5 is replaced with the more powerful ResNet50, to enhance feature extraction capabilities. In addition to detect minute garbage more effectively, a dedicated small object detection layer is added, along with a corresponding feature extraction and fusion module. Furthermore, by removing the original large and medium object detection heads, the waste of computational resources is reduced, thereby accelerating the model's inference speed. Overall, NWD is introduced in place of the IoU loss function, further enhancing the detection accuracy for small objects. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved model excels in the task of service area litter detection, achieving an mAP0.5 of 91.95% and a 5.02% increase compared to the original YOLOv5s model, with a detection rate of up to 72 frames per second. Compared to other mainstream object detection models, the method of this study shows superior performance in both detection accuracy and inference speed.

articleTitle: 95598 Network Traffic Prediction Based on CNN-BiLSTM-Attention Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In order to accurately predict short-term fluctuations in network traffic and improve the traffic monitoring performance of the 95598 customer service hotline network, this article combines convolutional neural networks (CNN), bidirectional long short-term memory networks (BiLSTM), and attention mechanisms (Attention) to input various traffic related influencing factors, and constructs a deep network model for CNN BiLSTM Attention network traffic prediction. Multiple traffic related influencing factors are input, Comprehensive construction of a deep network model for small-scale network traffic prediction. The experimental results show that compared with traditional shallow neural network prediction models and deep network LSTM prediction models, the method proposed in the article not only achieves higher accuracy in short-term traffic prediction, but also achieves better results in longer time series traffic prediction.

Author Keywords: Bidirectional Long Short Term Memory Network

articleTitle: Recent advances in integrated sensing and communication: a synergistic perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) is considered as a key technology in future wireless systems due to its advantages such as efficient spectrum utilization and the ability to reduce hardware cost. However, ISAC faces the problems of inherent conflicts between communication and sensing functions, performance degradation under non-line-of-sight, and high computational complexity of algorithms in ISAC systems. To address the inherent conflict between communication and sensing functions in ISAC, we overview the performance tradeoffs in ISAC. In response to the performance decay of ISAC under non-line-of-sight and the high computational complexity of its algorithms, we review the application of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) and deep learning techniques to Integrated Sensing and Communications (ISAC) and analyze their latest results and their great potential to enhance the performance of ISAC sensing and communications. Finally, we propose a new direction to further synergize the three techniques into an artificial intelligence-driven RIS-assisted ISAC technology, which provides useful guidance for future research.

articleTitle: Non-invasive blood glucose estimation based on fractional Fourier transform
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Diabetes is one of the popular chronic diseases in the world. The long term diabetes increases the risk of the stroke, the heart diseases, the kidney damage and the blindness. Therefore, the blood glucose estimation is crucial for the diabetic patients. The photoplethesmograms (PPGs) can be used for performing the non-invasive blood glucose estimation. In particular, the features were extracted from the PPG represented in both the time domain and the frequency domain. Nevertheless, the total number of the features was very limited. Hence, the performance of the blood glucose estimation was poor. To address this issue, this paper proposes to employ the fractional Fourier transform for extracting the features in the rotated time frequency domain. Since more than one rotational angle can be performed and a set of features can be extracted from each rotational angle, the total number of the features is significantly increased. The computer numerical simulations are conducted. Compared to the method only using the time domain features and the frequency domain features, it is found that the conventional method without the fractional Fourier transform domain features yields 77.2% of all the test data in the Zone A of the grid, respectively. On the other group, our proposed method with the fractional Fourier transform domain features yields 88.6% of all the test data in the Zone A of the grid, respectively. This demonstrates the superiority of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Image Recognition Based on Improved YOLOv5s Network Model Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In order to achieve rapid classification and extraction of pig target features. Propose an improved pig image object detection method based on YOLOv5s, using YOLOv5s adaptive anchor box calculation to obtain anchor boxes suitable for self built datasets; Combining convolutional block attention module to extract feature backbone network, improving model detection performance and reducing parameters. The Mosaic data augmentation method was used to enhance the image richness of the dataset and enhance the feature fusion ability of the network model. The improved algorithm was compared with the original YOLOv5s algorithm on a self-made dataset for ablation experiments. The results showed that the mean mAP of the improved algorithm reached 0.952, which showed a significant improvement in detection accuracy compared to other mainstream algorithms.

articleTitle: Neural Radiance Fields For Ultrasound Imaging with Image-to-Image Refinements
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Novel view synthesis in ultrasound imaging enables clinicians to visualize additional perspectives from existing scans, enhancing the interpretation of complex anatomical features without the need for further imaging. Traditional methods, however, often lead to compromised image quality, manifesting as blurring and loss of detail. In this study, we introduce an advanced framework that integrates neural radiance fields (NeRF) with generative adversarial networks (GANs) to produce ultrasound images with enhanced detail and improved tissue clarity. This framework combines the physics-informed neural representations of NeRF for initial image generation with a GAN-driven refinement process to improve image quality. Our comprehensive qualitative and quantitative evaluations demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance compared to existing techniques.

articleTitle: BiLSTM model with Attention mechanism for multi-label news text classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Multi-label text classification is very important in text research. A news will have multiple classification labels, and the number of labels is uncertain, so how to accurately learn labels from text is difficult. In this paper, GloVe is used for vectorization, and BiLSTM is used to learn the context, Use the Attention mechanism to focus on important words in the sentence, and finally focal loss function is used as the loss function. The experimental results show that the accuracy of this method reaches 84,43%% and AUR rate is 95.98%, which are higher than the evaluation scores of other five models.

articleTitle: Sparse Reduced-dimension Clutter Suppression Method Based on Multi-domain Joint Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: To improve the heterogeneous clutter suppression performance of airborne radar, a fast sparse reduced-dimension method based on multi-domain joint processing is proposed in this paper. Firstly, spatial diversity is adopted among transmitting sub-apertures to realize reduced dimension of spatial domain. Secondly, multiple equivalent samples are obtained by matching reconstruction. Thirdly, the dimension of these samples is further reduced based on energy transform domain. Finally, the clutter is suppressed by joint sparse recovery, and simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of proposal.

articleTitle: Kernel Extreme Learning Machine bearing fault diagnosis based on empirical wavelet transform feature extraction and Sparrow search algorithm optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Bearings are installed on mechanical equipment, and the environment of mechanical equipment is usually very noisy, and the vibration signal propagation path is very complex, so that the signal is always not pure enough, it is difficult to extract useful information, and the identification of faults brings some difficulties. It is proposed to use empirical wavelet transform to decompose fault signals, extract kurtosis as fault features, and input the established fault feature vector into a SSA-KELM for training and testing. According to experimental evidence, the method proposed in this article can quickly and better distinguish the fault state of the bearing at this time, which can bring many conveniences to our production and life. Compared with unoptimized kernel extreme learning machines, it has fast convergence speed and strong optimization ability.

articleTitle: A Neural Network and Bloom Filter-Based Name Search Method in Named Data Networking
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In a new network architecture like NDN, designing an efficient name lookup method has always been a valuable challenge. The paper studies the name lookup technology based on the Bloom filter and BPNN neural network mapping model in named data networking. In the part of the hybrid model based on the Bloom filter and BPNN, the paper proposes the fusion idea of the Bloom filter and BPNN, and provides a detailed introduction to the construction process of the hybrid model. At the same time, in order to improve the memory utilization of traditional Bloom filters, this article proposes a way to use neural networks to enhance it, and proved its effectiveness through experiments.

articleTitle: Research on Geographical Routing in Aeronautical Ad hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This study addresses the inadequacies in the consideration of specific technological environments in the research of geographical routing for Aeronautical Ad hoc Networks (AANETs). It focuses on analyzing the performance of two geographical routing algorithms, Greedy Perimeter Stateless Routing (GPSR) and Geographic Load Share Routing (GLSR), under the combined conditions of single-beam directional antennas and Spatial Time Division Multiple Access (STDMA) link scheduling. Firstly, an AANET model incorporating single-beam directional antennas and STDMA link scheduling is established, and the time slot allocation is optimized using a simulated annealing algorithm. Secondly, the principles of the GPSR and GLSR algorithms are analyzed in detail based on this model. Lastly, the performance of both GPSR and GLSR algorithms is verified through simulation. The study demonstrates that, in the specific technological environment of AANETs considering single-beam directional antennas and STDMA link scheduling, the GLSR algorithm markedly outperforms GPSR by tripling node throughput and reducing average end-to-end delay by 80%.

articleTitle: Cross-Modal Noise Information Elimination Network for Medical Visual Question Answering
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Medical Visual Question Answering (Med-VQA) aims to answer clinical questions given medical images and deduce the best answer. The existing Med-VQA models fuse question and image features by the dense interactions between each image region and each question. However, the existing Med-VQA methods ignore the noise information generated by the interactions between the image regions unrelated and the question words unrelate, but these noise information interfere with the inference of the model. We propose a Cross-Modal Noise Information Elimination Network (CMNIEN) for medical visual question answering. Firstly, question features are extracted by the BERT model, and image features are extracted by the ResNet network; Then, the question and image features were concatenated together, and a threshold based feature fusion module for Med-VQA was designed to eliminate the noise information generated by the interaction of different modal features of images and questions; Finally, a cross modal self attention module is used to enhance the attention of key features. Extensive experiments were conducted on the Med-VQA-2019 and VQA-RAD datasets, and the results showed that each improvement can effectively enhance model performance. When the threshold is set to 0.1, the overall accuracy of the model on the Med-VQA-2019 dataset reaches 81.9%, and the overall accuracy on the VQA-RAD dataset reaches 77.2%.

articleTitle: Gesture Recognition Method Based on Computer Vision and Surface Electromyography : Implementing Intention Recognition of the Healthy Side in the Hand Assessment Process
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the rapid development of sensing technology, a variety of hand rehabilitation assessment systems have emerged as choices for patients engaged in home-based rehabilitation. However, challenges such as fixed assessment sequences and operational constraints persist. To enhance the efficiency of hand rehabilitation assessment systems, employing gesture recognition to detect the healthy side's movement intent for assisting in the evaluation is a viable solution. In recent years, significant improvements have been made in gesture recognition methods, with some based on computer vision(CV) and surface electromyography(sEMG) demonstrating promising results. This paper explores a gesture recognition method based on both CV and sEMG. Initially, image data and surface electromyographic signals are collected, and joint coordinate data is extracted using the Mediapipe API. Subsequently, both sets of data undergo preprocessing and feature extraction, followed by training random forest(RF) and Convolutional Neural Network(CNN) classifiers separately. A weighted decision-making approach is then employed, achieving a commendable performance in gesture recognition, with an accuracy rate of 96.66%.
