In this paper, we use Cross-Supervised Learning to train a model on three different datasets, which can concurrently perform human detection, keypoint detection, human part parsing and densepose estimation. We also study the transfer learning relations across three datasets, and exploit them to improve performance in the most efficient way. It is noteworthy that we don’t need to optimize the model structure, and we can achieve state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks.

articleTitle: A Low-Resource-Cost FPGA Implementation of Population Threshold Coding for Spiking Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Spike encoding plays a vital role in the advancement of neuromorphic computing as the spike sequences represent the information of raw data. Both rate coding and temporal coding algorithms have been established either with one neuron or with a population of neurons. To facilitate the development of end-to-end neuromorphic computing, this work presents a low-resource-cost Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) implementation of speech signal feature extraction and spike encoding. Based on the MEL spectrum features of speech, a feature extraction circuit of the normalized logarithmic spectrum and a population threshold coding (PTC) circuit are designed to achieve low resource cost. The proposed design was verified through the TIDIGITS dataset. The generated spike sequences were input to a spatial-temporal backpropagation (STBP) based spiking neural network (SNN) classifier, which achieves a competitive classification performance compared with existing spike coding schemes and shows 95.35% accuracy.

articleTitle: Compact, Optimized, and Effective: The CNNSpectra Approach to Deep Learning in Spectral Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Deep learning has been instrumental in advancing various fields, including spectral data analysis. However, it is essential to recognize that deep layers and complex networks are not always prerequisites for achieving superior performance results. In this context, we introduce CNNSpectra, a simplified yet highly optimized deep learning model tailored for spectral data analysis, particularly for assessing food quality from portable spectroscopic devices. CNNSpectra’s performance is comprehensively evaluated on diverse datasets, including flour powders, spices, and chocolate, collected across multiple sessions. The results demonstrate that CNNSpectra consistently achieves competitive performance levels across various spectral datasets. While it may not outperform the best machine learning models in all cases, its simplicity and optimization render it a promising approach for real-world spectral data analysis, offering a valuable tool for food quality assessment from portable devices. This work underscores the importance of exploring more efficient and effective deep learning models in spectral data analysis and opens avenues for future research and improvements in this domain.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-objective Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem Based on Improved Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In the contemporary field of production management, the Flexible Job Shop Scheduling Problem (FJSP) emerges as a pivotal research topic, originating from the traditional job shop scheduling problem. In FJSP, each operation of a job can be processed by different machines, and each machine is capable of handling a variety of operations. This study constructs a multi-objective scheduling model, taking into account various factors prevalent in real-world production, such as the operating time, load, and energy consumption of machines. Addressing the limited convergence of the existing NSGA2 algorithm, this research integrates a variable neighborhood search algorithm to enhance the local search capability of the original algorithm, effectively avoiding the pitfall of local optima. To resolve the issue of low-quality initial solutions due to the random initialization of the NSGA2 algorithm, this study introduces a population initialization strategy based on heuristic rules, thereby improving the quality of initial solutions and accelerating the iterative optimization process. Comparative simulations with other heuristic rules and various intelligent algorithms demonstrate the efficiency of the improved NSGA2 algorithm in finding high-quality solutions. The application of the modified NSGA2 algorithm to real-life cases not only successfully addresses the issues of magnitude and dimensions among different objectives but also yields a satisfying set of Pareto solutions, further confirming the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed algorithm and model.

articleTitle: An AdaptiveSMOTE-RF algorithm for unbalanced data classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The SMOTE algorithm selects a neighborhood near a minor sample and ignores the distribution characteristics of a small number of samples. This marginalizes the minority samples and affects the model’s classification performance. To mitigate this, Adaptive-SMOTE and random forest feature selection are combined to reduce the impact of data imbalance during data pre-processing. In the data pre-processing stage, the adaptive and heavy-sampling SMOTE algorithm determines the sampling ratio from synthetic samples in an adaptive manner to better control the sampling process. Next, optimal features are selected through random forest feature selection methods, and each tree is assigned a corresponding weight. This empowers trees with better classification capabilities, giving them greater voting influence during the voting stage and enhancing the random forest algorithm’s overall classification performance. Experiments on the Kaggle dataset demonstrate that, compared to the original algorithm, the improved algorithm enhances the accuracy and overall sample classification performance of the minority samples.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Polar Positioning Performance of GNSS based on STK
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In order to grasp the positioning performance of the four major global satellite navigation systems in the polar region, the standard constellations of the four systems were constructed using STK software. Through simulations of the visible satellites count, GDOP, navigation accuracy, and other indicators at seven typical stations in the polar region, the performance advantages and disadvantages of the four systems were statistically analyzed. The results showed that GALILEO had the best positioning performance at typical stations in the polar region, GPS performed the worst, and China's self-developed BDS belonged to the upper middle level.

articleTitle: A log parsing method based on non-fixed search tree
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Log data records important information about the system during operation, and plays an important role in system anomaly detection. As the size of logs continues to increase, efficiently processing logs has become an important issue. In this paper, we propose a log parsing method called CUD, which is based on a non-fixed search tree. The method encodes log parsing rules in a structural tree format and parses log messages, and is tested on four publicly available log datasets. Experimental results show that compared to other online methods, CUD has higher accuracy and achieves efficient and accurate parsing of log data.

articleTitle: Robot visual perception and autonomous obstacle avoidance based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Dynamic obstacle avoidance is crucial for a robot to achieve autonomous and safe navigation, especially in complex and ever-changing indoor environments. The robot needs to detect obstacles in a timely manner and dynamically plan a safe path. To accomplish this, an environment perception system is established using an RGB-D depth camera and an IMU unit, providing the robot with multimodal information such as 3D vision and orientation angles. Firstly, an improved target detection model based on YOLOv7-tiny is constructed. This model utilizes the YOLOv7-tiny algorithm to recognize obstacles in color images. The color and depth images are aligned to obtain obstacle size information and spatial distance between the robot and obstacles. The synchronized color and depth information are then inputted into the RTAB-D SLAM algorithm to construct a map. After mapping, the DWA local path planning algorithm is used to plan a path, and obstacle avoidance decisions are sent to the chassis control module to achieve autonomous obstacle avoidance. This enables the robot to navigate autonomously in real-world scenarios. Experimental analysis shows that the improved YOLOv7-tiny target detection algorithm achieves slightly higher accuracy compared to the original algorithm, with a 25% increase in FPS during detection. The proposed method successfully enables the robot to achieve autonomous obstacle avoidance. This research provides a basis and reference for robots to rely solely on visual and inertial sensors for obstacle recognition and autonomous navigation.

articleTitle: Typhoon Track Image Prediction Using a Comprehensive LSTM Attention Model in Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Typhoons are exceptionally destructive tropical cyclones that possess the capacity to inflict significant harm upon society. For institutions engaged in risk assessment and disaster mitigation, accurately forecasting typhoon paths and trajectories is of paramount importance. In this study, we propose a Typhoon Track Image Prediction model based on a Comprehensive Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) Attention Model in the field of Deep Learning. This model significantly improves the accuracy of typhoon track prediction. To assess its performance, we utilize typhoon data from the China Typhoon Network spanning from 1949 to 2022. The Comprehensive LSTM Attention Model is compared against other popular models such as Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN), traditional LSTM, and Seq2Seq models for forecasting the typhoon track over a 12-hour period. The results demonstrate the superiority of our proposed model, showcasing its effectiveness in terms of superior accuracy in typhoon track prediction.

articleTitle: Research on multi-base station operation cost optimization based on multi-dimensional utility function
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the rapid growth of mobile communication system traffic, it is urgent to carry out related research to alleviate the power consumption of base stations (BSs). It is used to realize the matching of information flow and energy flow of communication system, and to complete the accurate matching of communication service and BS renewable energy (RE) reserve. In this paper, a multi-dimensional utility function (MDUF) is constructed to optimize the multi-BS system by solving the problem of maximizing the utility value of the MDUF. The optimization problem is divided into three sub-problems : user scheduling, power allocation and BS load balancing. The problem is solved iteratively by using alternating optimization and continuous convex approximation techniques. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm improves the utilization rate of RE by 58.68 % and 29.74 % respectively, and the total cost of the system has been maintained at a low level, which has significant advantages.

articleTitle: MSFE-CapsNet: a Multiscale Feature-enhanced Capsule Network for Skin Lesion Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Automatic classification of skin lesion images is an important method for learning lesion characteristics from dermoscopic images and determining the category to which they belong, which is crucial for the diagnosis and treatment of skin cancer. However, the large variation in lesion size seriously affects the classification of the images. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a Multiscale feature-enhanced capsule network (MSFE-CapsNet), which employs a large size 31 × 31 convolutional kernel to obtain a larger perceptual domain, and design a multiscale feature enhancement block to augment the local feature information to further learn the semantic information of the lesion image, and finally introduces the Efficient Multi-Scale Attention to efficiently obtain spatial location information of skin lesions on a high-level feature map. The experimental results show that MSFE-CapsNet achieves 95.05% accuracy on the HAM10000 dataset, which is better than the existing methods for skin lesion classification, and has only 1.58M parameters.

articleTitle: Lightweight Children's Expression Recognition Network Based on Multi-scale Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems that ordinary convolutional neural network is difficult to extract effective features and network model parameters are complex in children's expression recognition, a lightweight expression recognition network with multi-scale attention mechanism is proposed. First, in order to increase the width and depth of the network and avoid redundant calculations, the Inception structure is introduced into the network to extract multi-scale feature information of images. Then, the Channel Attention mechanism is used to emphasize the areas related to facial expressions and suppress the irrelevant background areas, so as to improve the model's ability to represent important feature information. In addition, depthwise separable convolution is used in the convolutional layer to reduce network parameters and prevent overfitting. The experimental results show that the method has better recognition effect and stronger generalization ability, and has certain reference value for network structure setting and parameter configuration in facial expression recognition.

articleTitle: Design and Rapid Emergency Strategy of Satellite-Ground Integrated Communication Network Based on the Characteristics of Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In response to the requirements of stable operation of power grid management and rapid response to power emergency communication events, this article proposes a design concept for satellite-ground integrated communication network configuration, optimizes ground network design, and utilizes the relay capability of communication satellites to improve the overall operational capability and emergency response level of the system. Firstly, consider the ground communication layout of power grid construction, fully considering factors such as load balancing, construction location, coverage range, construction cost and probability of disaster occurrence of ground communication stations. Through weighting optimization combined with K-Means regional segmentation method, provide the optimal regional management method under normal conditions. Secondly, based on the characteristics of satellite wide area coverage, a fast self-organizing network relay method is proposed. When a node encounters disasters or other situations, the satellite is used to quickly complete the relay, avoiding communication interruptions between nodes. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm proposed in this paper was verified through simulation experiments. In various situations, the emergency response coverage rate of the algorithm has reached over 95% while ensuring the load balancing.

articleTitle: Volume-Wise Decoding of Human Brain's Task fMRI via Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In recent years, significant progress has been made in decoding human cognitive tasks from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) images using deep learning methods. However, existing approaches predominantly rely on the assumption of temporal stationarity of neural activity, decoding static brain networks from task-based fMRI data at the block-wise. The study of dynamic brain networks poses challenges in terms of limited accuracy and complexity of research methods. This limitation hampers the development of neuroscience in achieving a broader and finer-grained understanding of human brain function across a wider range of temporal scales. To address this issue, we propose an volume-wise decoder for task fMRI, adopts end-to-end deep learning method. Compared with traditional machine learning methods, the decoding accuracy and efficiency are significantly improved. This method not only offers a more accurate and efficient decoding approach for a finer-grained comprehension of cognitive processes, but also offers new perspectives and insights into human cognition.

articleTitle: Resource Allocation Method for 5G Communication System Based on ICHOA
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the advancement of the commercial process of the fifth generation (5G) mobile communication systems, device to device (D2D) communication has attracted more and more attention. In order to solve the problems of high computational complexity and poor allocation optimization effect of existing 5G communication system resource allocation algorithms. This article proposes a resource allocation optimization method for 5G network D2D communication system based on the improved Chimp Optimization Algorithm (ICHOA). It introduces hunting contribution weighting and improves the convergence factor on the basis of traditional algorithms to improve the optimization performance of the algorithm. The proposed method is verified through simulation examples. The results show that the proposed improvement strategy improves the optimization performance of the resource allocation algorithm, effectively improving the system’s throughput on limited resources and reducing various channel interferences within the system.

articleTitle: MMLoc: A Multi-instance Multi-label Learning Approach for Predicting Protein Subcellular Localization from Immunofluorescence Images
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The emergence and development of immunofluorescence (IF) imaging techniques offers the opportunity to observe protein distribution and localization at the cellular level, which is critical for revealing cellular mechanisms and disease pathology. Deep learning-based artificial intelligence technologies have played an important role in advancing the field of IF image recognition by harnessing these techniques. However, using deep neural networks to directly predict protein localization (PSL) in these complex images remains extremely challenging, especially when dealing with proteins that exhibit multiple localizations across heterogeneous cell populations within the same sample. To address this challenge, we formulate the PSL modeling problem as a Multi-Instance Multi-Label (MIML) learning task and propose a novel PSL model named MMLoc. Specifically, considering an IF image contains multiple cells, we utilize U-Net to segment the IF image and treat each cell as an instance, making this method especially suitable for scenarios where the image possesses multiple labels simultaneously and exhibits single-cell variation. On this basis, we employ a pre-trained ResNet50 model to extract features from instances, integrating a self-attention mechanism to focus on the most discriminative features. After fusing these instances, we connect them through a traditional fully connected classifier for predicting the protein localization class. The experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance on a challenging HPA dataset.

articleTitle: Cross-domain recommendation based on meta-networks and attention transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Although cross-domain recommendation systems play a crucial role in solving the data sparseness and cold start challenges in recommendation systems, current algorithms primarily rely on the user-item rating matrix for user feature modeling, leading to sparse data. Furthermore, existing cross-domain recommendation algorithms employ mapping transfer methods that result in negative migration issues. This negative migration significantly impacts the capability of cross-domain recommendation systems. Therefore, this paper presents a novel cross-domain recommendation algorithm based on meta-network and attention transfer. In the algorithm, we first utilize pre-trained user embedding information to generate user features within their respective domains. We introduce a reconstructed self-encoder to generate global user embeddings, enhancing the user representation for users in the source and target domain. Next, we leverage the user/item interaction information of the user in the source field to generate migratable user feature information through a meta-network. Finally, through the attention network, we use the user feature embeddings of the target field and the user's migratable information in the source field as the input of the attention network to generate feature embeddings specific to the target field for rating prediction. We conducted experiments on two domain pairs consisting of three Amazon datasets. The results indicate that the algorithm presented in this paper outperforms other benchmark models under MSE and MAE evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: Research on Spatial Energy Distribution of Wideband Distributed Coherent Aperture Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The coherent area formed by coherent emission of wideband distributed coherent aperture radar (DCAR) will affect the performance of coherent detection for the multi-scattering-point targets. However, the distribution regularities of the coherent area haven’t been investigated yet. In this paper, the spatial energy distribution formed by DCAR is firstly investigated through theoretical derivations and simulations, so as to determine the distribution regularities of the coherent area. The results show that the size of the coherent area is proportional to the target distance, whereas inversely proportional to the center frequency of the transmitting waveform, the antenna spacing, and the number of the unit radars. The research in this paper provides guidance for the layout of DCAR system, which are of great importance for the coherent detection of the multi-scattering-point targets.

articleTitle: Massive Parallel Simulation for Tensor Network Contraction Ordering Solving
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Tensor network contraction is a powerful mathematical tool for dealing with complex systems and high-dimensional data, which is widely used in classical simulations of molecules and quantum circuits. To improve the performance of simulations, existing methods are implemented by searching the optimal contraction orderings for tensor networks. In particular, some reinforcement learning (RL) methods show a greater potential for solving. However, with the increasing scale of simulation, the number of tensors in the corresponding tensor network is huge, the existing RL methods suffer from sampling bottlenecks and slow solving speed, which make it difficult to efficiently solve for high-quality contraction orderings. In this paper, we design a massive parallel simulation environment for tensor network contraction ordering solving on a single GPU. We experimented with multiple numbers of parallel environments on the tensor-train network, and achieved the highest speedup when the number of environments was 2<sup>6</sup>. We also have experimented on large-scale tensor-train networks and tree tensor networks, and compared to Kahypar and RL-Baseline, our method achieves average speedup of 8.96× and 7.48× on tensor-train networks, and 10.03× and 7.48× on tree tensor networks.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Medical Image Diagnostic Network Deployed on Low-Cost Embedded Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Early diagnosis of brain tumors is of great significance to patients, families, and society. Therefore, it is necessary to develop more accurate, fast, and reliable diagnostic methods for brain tumors. Deep learning based brain tumor diagnosis technology has great application prospects and is expected to play an important role in early diagnosis and treatment of brain tumors. This article proposes a lightweight deep learning model guided by attention mechanism. Training and testing were conducted on two publicly available brain tumor datasets, and compared with state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results show that the classification accuracy of this method is 99.8 %, which is higher than state-of-the-art methods. This has created a new state-of-the-art diagnostic method for brain tumors. The method proposed in this article is fast, robust, with low network computing complexity and low memory requirements. It can be deployed on low-cost embedded devices and has great application prospects in the medical field.

articleTitle: An lightweight multimodal segmentation network for white matter tracts
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The brain's white matter tracts are significant for preoperative planning and postoperative prediction of brain surgery, as their lesions can be observed to diagnose the condition and promptly develop treatment plans. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is the mainstream brain imaging method, and T1-weighted (T1w) images generated by scanning are often used to map white matter tracts. However, most of the current brain white matter tract studies are limited to mapping white matter tract trajectories, and little is known about the white matter tract's volume, making it difficult for physicians to make a correct judgment. Based on the above problems, we propose a multimodal lightweight 3D end-to-end framework Attention Vnet-Tiny (AVnet-T) to segment brain white matter tracts accurately. AVnet-T (1) parallelizes two different-sized 3D convolution operations at the input layer, enabling more comprehensive extraction of white matter tract features in multi-modal imaging; (2) introduces compression and activation attention in the encoder part to dynamically adjust the weights to ensure that fiber flow features are not lost in compressing resolution information and aggregating semantic information; (3) significantly reduces the number of its parameters and speeds up its convergence speed when maintaining the performance. We used the BrainPTM2021 challenge online validation tool to evaluate our model with an average dice coefficient of 0.7072. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed model is efficient and lightweight in automating the segmentation of brain white matter tracts.

articleTitle: Efficient Lightweight Multiscale Attention Network for Image Steganalysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the combination of deep learning, steganography is becoming more and more resistant to steganalysis, making it more and more difficult for traditional steganalysis to extract features from steganographic images. In this paper, we address the above problems and propose an efficient lightweight image steganalysis method (ELMANet) based on cascaded multiscale neural networks and the multiscale hybrid attention mechanism to extract more significant features from steganographic images. The architecture of ELMANet comprises three integral components: a preprocessing module, a feature extraction module, and a classification module. Through rigorous experimental validation on different datasets, ELMANet performs better in terms of steganalysis detection accuracy, while requiring lower network parameters and computational resource overheads compared to existing image steganalysis models.

articleTitle: Dempster-Shafer Theory Empowered Deep Learning for Enhanced 3D PET-CT Medical Image Segmentation: A first test on Automated Lesion Segmentation in Whole-body Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In recent years, the fusion of deep learning with Dempster-Shafer Theory has shown great promise in medical image analysis, particularly for its capacity to model uncertainty and enhance accuracy. This paper presents an ongoing study utilizing deep evidential networks for Lymphoma segmentation in three-dimensional Positron Emission Tomography (PET) and Computed Tomography (CT) images. Expanding on the Evidential Neural Network U-Net (ENN-UNet), which integrates UNet with Dempster-Shafer Theory, we explore various feature extractors (3D-UNet, V-Net, 3D ResNet, HighRes3DNet, 3D DenseNet, and DeepMedic) incorporated into a Dempster-Shafer layer to boost segmentation results. Our primary experiments, focusing on ENN-based segmentation methods (ENN-UNet and ENN-VNet), conducted on a mixed dataset of 501 samples, encompassing melanoma, lymphoma, and lung cancer, reveal that the inclusion of an evidential layer can enhance the model's performance in complex tasks.

articleTitle: A Channel Prediction Scheme Under The Condition of Incomplete History
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, when user movement causes serious channel aging, it requires the use of channel prediction to solve the problem that channel estimation cannot obtain real-time channel state information (CSI). However, the existing work is based on the assumption of obtaining a perfect historical sequence, without considering the problem of incomplete history caused by pilot signal spacing. The method of filling in the incomplete value with the predicted value will cause the prediction error to accumulate and affect the final performance. In this paper, we propose an interpolation scheme based on the variational autoencoder (VAE) to generate incomplete value that conforms to the distribution of historical sequence data, thereby restoring the channel dynamic information in historical sequences. In addition, we design a prediction module based on complex residual network, which effectively captures the correlation between the real and imaginary parts of the CSI sequence as well as the spatiotemporal correlation. Experimental results verify the superiority of the proposed framework in prediction performance.

articleTitle: Minimizing Age of Information by Deep Reinforcement Learning for Next Generation Multiple Access
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In the next generation of multiple access, with the explosive growth of multimedia communication services and the emergence of new application scenarios, the timeliness of information has become the main goal for the future. And age of information (AoI) has been proposed to indicate the freshness of information. It is crucial to explore a channel access policy that optimizes AoI under feasible mechanisms in order to better improve the timeliness of the system. However, such channel access policy and corresponding mechanism are basically unknown. In recent years, the rapid advancement of machine learning, especially deep reinforcement learning (DRL), has provided promising solutions to address this challenge. Therefore, this article considers the problem of multiple access and aims to minimize the average AoI of the entire network. To achieve this idea, we first represent it as a decentralized Markov decision process (Dec-MDP). Then we propose a deep Q-network (DQN) based algorithm to help distributed nodes make access decisions independently, such that the freshness of network information could be improved. The corresponding simulations were finally conducted, and the results indicate that the DQN based policy can reduce global average AoI to a certain extent.

articleTitle: Rotation-Invariant LiDAR-based Localization Method Based on Feature Pyramid and Vector Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: LiDAR-based localization for unmanned vehicle has recently become a highly prominent research area. The LiDAR-based localization task typically involves two crucial tasks: place recognition and pose estimation. However, current research often fails to effectively address issues of place recognition retrieval failures caused by rotations. Some existing methods employ a strategy of coupling the pose estimation task with location recognition, but they often separate these two tasks using two distinct sets of networks to achieve robustness against rotations. Unfortunately, such methods frequently exhibit poor generalization. In this paper, we propose an innovative rotation-invariant LiDAR-based localization method based on feature pyramids and vector neural networks. This approach extracts rotation-invariant global features to accomplish the location recognition task and utilizes rotation-invariant local features for matching corresponding points in point clouds. Employing a coarse-to-fine point matching filtering method to eliminate outliers, and ultimately implementing pose estimation through the RANSAC algorithm, we successfully achieve high-precision and rotation-robust LiDAR-based localization. The experiments indicate that on the Oxford dataset, our method consistently achieves a remarkable 94.7% AR@1% regardless of whether the point cloud undergoes rotation, a performance significantly superior to other methods

articleTitle: Indoor Fire Prediction Based On the CEEMDAN-LSTM-CNN Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Gas indicators such as carbon monoxide, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and compressed natural gas (CNG) are often affected and changed during indoor fire events. However, the prediction accuracy is reduced due to the small trend of these metrics and the insignificant difference between the extreme values and minima. To solve this problem, a coupled model for fire indicators based on complete ensemble empirical modal decomposition (CEEMDAN), convolutional neural network (CNN), and long and short-term memory neural network (LSTM) is proposed. This model was applied to the prediction of gas indicators affected by fire, the prediction results of this model were compared with those of other models. The experimental findings demonstrate enhanced accuracy in predicting changes in gas indicators and a closer alignment with actual results through our model, offering a potent solution for indoor fire prevention.

articleTitle: Product selection method based on feature level fusion of heterogeneous product data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: To enable e-commerce sellers to identify products favoured by consumer groups and thereby increase their store's sales and profit margins, a product classification model based on feature-level fusion of heterogeneous data is proposed. The model uses a convolutional neural network to learn feature representations from product title, descriptions and reviews. It also uses a deep autoencoder to learn feature representations from product attributes. By combining the features of heterogeneous data, a comprehensive representation of the product is obtained. Experiments were conducted using data from all basketball products on the Amazon e-commerce platform. The results of the experiments showed that building a product classification model based on heterogeneous data outperformed using only product title. The accuracy of the model improved by 3.13% and the F1 score increased by 4.54%. These results strongly suggest that the product classification model based on heterogeneous data has learned more comprehensive features related to product popularity.

articleTitle: Research on Classification and Prediction of General Traffic Accidents on National and Provincial Highways Based on BP Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the continuous increase in the number of motor vehicles in China, the problem of traffic safety is becoming more and more prominent, and traffic accidents occur frequently, in order to understand the probability of accidents and possible impacts, this paper proposes a classification prediction method for general traffic accidents on national and provincial roads based on BP neural network. The data of traffic accidents on national and provincial roads from 2018 to 2020 are classified by the characteristics of the influencing factors, and the data are divided into a test machine and a validation set to train the BP neural network model, and the neural network models with one hidden layer and two hidden layers are evaluated by the confusion matrix, and the results show that the BP neural network model with one hidden layer is shorter in time consumption, and the difference in the accuracy of the model is not very large, so the BP neural network model with one hidden layer is more accurate. layer BP neural network model is more suitable for the classification prediction of general traffic accidents on national and provincial highways. In this paper, the BP neural network-based classification prediction method of general traffic accidents on national and provincial highways is of great significance to reduce the occurrence of accidents and the risk of accidents.

articleTitle: A Vector Similarity-based Knowledge Graph Embedding Method for Predicting Missing Hierarchical Relationships in SNOMED CT
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: SNOMED CT, as the largest clinical terminology set globally, serves as a vital knowledge source for numerous downstream applications. The accuracy and comprehensiveness of its domain knowledge significantly impact related applications. Among the crucial relationships within SNOMED CT, hierarchical relationships play a fundamental role in shaping the framework and structure of the terminology set. However, the inherent incompleteness of these relationships has been a limiting factor in the development of applications in the field. Therefore, automating the discovery of missing hierarchical relationships in this terminology set holds great significance and has garnered extensive attention from researchers. Most existing methods for this task primarily focus on the lexical features of concepts while overlooking the critical role of knowledge graph embedding methods. In this paper, we propose a knowledge graph embedding approach that can predict missing hierarchical relationships in the terminology set without relying on lexical features. To the best of our knowledge, our method is the first to introduce knowledge graph embedding to this task and demonstrate its effectiveness. Our model can learn low-dimensional vector representations that capture the specificity of nodes and relationships, as well as the joint embedding representations of nodes and relationships in the graph structure. We evaluate the proposed approach using a vector similarity prediction function on the US edition of SNOMED CT and achieve an F1 score of 97.80%. The experimental results demonstrate that our model can accurately predict missing hierarchical relationships between concepts, offering valuable guidance for completing the missing hierarchical relationships.

articleTitle: The Effect of Coherent Frequency Diverse Array on Watson-Watt Direction-Finding System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Frequency diverse array(FDA) offer potential applications for enhancing the RF safety performance of FDA systems. This is due to the time-varying angle-distance coupling characteristics of the transmit beam map, which are caused by small frequency shifts between subarray elements. In this paper, we investigate the impact of coherent FDA signals on amplitude-based direction-finding systems, taking the Watson-Watt direction-finding system as an example. Firstly, we establish receiving model for direction finding of FDA signals. Secondly, we evaluate the error of the direction-finding system when using coherent FDA signals and analyze it with the Cramér-Rao lower bound(CRLB). Finally, we conduct a simulation analysis to validate the proposed theory. Both the theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate that coherent FDA signals can improve the radio frequency(RF) stealth performance. Specifically, the analysis and simulation results reveal that coherent FDA signals exhibit superior low-intercept performance for the Watson-Watt direction-finding system. These findings can be applied to all amplitude direction-finding systems.

articleTitle: A Perturbed Convolutional Layer and Gradient Normalization based Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper develops Perturbed Convolutional layers and Penalty Gradient Normalization based Generative Adversarial Network (PCPGN-GAN) to address the issues of training instability caused by sharp gradient space and the discriminator’s memorization problem. The distinctive aspect of the perturbation convolutional layer lies in its departure from traditional convolutional layer. It accomplishes this by introducing random perturbations to the input tensor before conducting convolution operations. This modification significantly reduces the discriminator’s inclination toward memorization issue. Moreover, the introduction of the penalty gradient norm constraint is exclusive to the discriminator function. This constraint enhances its capacity while stabilizing gradient information, thereby improving training stability. Comparative evaluations across multiple datasets, including CIFAR-10, STL-10, Tiny ImageNet, CelebA-HQ and LSUN-Church, highlight the superior performance of the PCPGN-GAN. Experimental results indicate its considerable advantages, manifesting in higher image quality and surpassing existed methods in terms of Inception Score and Frechet Inception Distance.

articleTitle: Biometric identification based on electrocardiogram Using Markov Transition Field and Hybrid Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Identification based on electrocardiogram (ECG) has attracted attention of researchers. One-dimension features of ECG signal are extracted and classified is effective in the rest state; however, the scheme performance in activity state is unsatisfactory. Because ECG waveform is influenced by the subject's emotional and physical states. To address ECG recognition during activity, an approach for personal identification of ECG, incorporating the first-order Markov chain and phase transform is proposed. The proposed approach involves the segmentation of ECG into sub-signals, each comprising multiple heartbeats, carrying rich feature information. Sub-signals are converted into images using the Markov Transition Field (MTF) Additionally, the Phase Transform (PT) algorithm is employed to unveil inter-beat information within ECG signals. For the generated images using the MTF method, a hybrid network, combining the wavelet scattering network (WSN) and Resnet, is employed for feature extraction and classification. The impact of sub-signal lengths and the utilization of the PT algorithm in capturing inter-class information on the recognition model's performance are discussed in experiments. The proposed method's feasibility is substantiated validation on two public datasets: ECG-ID and ECG-GUDB. In the ECG-ID dataset, the recognition system attains a commendable accuracy of 90.26%. In the ECG-GUDB dataset, assessments under various conditions reveal impressive performance, achieving 94.34% accuracy in the resting states, 93.17% in the moving states, and 92.73% accuracy in combined moving and resting states. These results surpass the performance of the majority of existing algorithms.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Atmospheric Laser Communication Turbo Code based on Improved MAX-Log-MAP Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The decoding performance of suboptimal MAX-Log-MAP algorithm is reduced due to neglecting the correction function. To solve the above problem, this paper proposes an optimization method that combines linear fitting of correction functions with the correction factors based on extrinsic information for atmospheric turbulence channels. A piecewise linear fitting correction function is used to reduce the calculation errors of the forward and backward recursion terms in the decoding, and the optimal correction factor is given to obtain accurate extrinsic information so as to achieve the minimum error performance of the system under the given SNR. The simulation results show that the improved algorithm achieves a gain of nearly 0.5dB compared with the Max-Log-MAP algorithm at a bit error rate of 10<sup>-6</sup>, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and can effectively improve the error correction performance of Turbo code in atmospheric laser communication system.

articleTitle: Joint Channel Estimation Based on the Structured Sparsity for FDD Massive MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The variability of wireless environment makes channel estimation increasingly important for 5G communications. However, the pilot overhead is high in massive multiple-input multiple-output systems. Thus, a joint channel estimation scheme based on the structured sparsity of the channel is proposed to reduce the pilot overhead. Specifically, the structured sparsity of the channel is revealed firstly, i.e., adjacent slots for a user enjoy the partially common non-zero rows in a channel matrix. Then, multiple time slots can be estimated jointly by exploiting this property. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can achieve accurate channel estimation with a low pilot overhead.

articleTitle: Residual Attention Mechanism-Based MRI Super-Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) super-resolution technology is a crucial research direction in the field of medical image processing. This paper aims to enhance the spatial resolution of MRI, improve image quality, and enhance the diagnostic capabilities of medical imaging. In this study, we first preprocess MR images to ensure the quality of input data. Subsequently, we designed a network, RPCN, based on a residual attention mechanism. This network adaptively focuses on important regions in MRI and employs the concept of residual learning to effectively capture high-frequency information for super-resolution reconstruction. In the RPCN network, we introduce a channel attention mechanism and a pixel attention mechanism, and design an attention-serial-fusion RPC structure to enable the network to more effectively explore correlations between different channels and better capture image features. Extensive experiments demonstrate the significant success of our method in enhancing MRI resolution. The introduction of residual structure and attention mechanisms allows our network to delve deeper into learning image details, enabling better reconstruction of image edges, textures, and microstructures. We also use quantitative evaluation metrics such as Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) to objectively assess the performance of the RPCN network structure. Multiple sets of comparative experiments validate its robustness and generality on different MRI datasets.

articleTitle: Wavelet Thresholding and Sliding Mean Filtering-Based Signal Denoising for Atomic Fluorescence Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Atomic fluorescence spectral signals usually contain noise, and the noise will affect the analysis of the signals, so it is necessary to process the spectral signals. Aiming at the characteristics of atomic fluorescence spectral signals, this paper proposes to denoise the signals by using wavelet transform combined with sliding mean filtering, which first denoises the signals by wavelet thresholding and then filters the signals by sliding mean filtering. The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), mean square error (MSE), and waveform similarity parameter (NCC), are used to evaluate the effectiveness of spectral signal processing, and the final experimental results show that the hybrid filtering method of wavelet threshold combined with moving mean can effectively remove the noise in the atomic fluorescence spectrum signal.

articleTitle: Highway traffic parameter prediction model based on the combined deep learning model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Traffic flow time series prediction is developing very rapidly. The research methods of prediction models mainly focus on model parameter optimization and data feature analysis to improve prediction accuracy. Based on this, this article adopts the form of model optimization and uses ETC gantry data to conduct optimal combination and applicability analysis of time series prediction models.This paper builds two deep learning time series combination prediction models based on the Internet of Vehicles and Internet of Things environments and combines them with current research results. Model 1 (INFO-LSTM) is an LSTM prediction model based on the vector-weighted optimization algorithm. Model 2 (ICSSA-GRU-ATT) is a GRU model based on the improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (ICSSA) under the attention mechanism. Short-term prediction was carried out using the ETC data of Shanlin Expressway in Gansu Province as the experimental content. The results showed that the data training and prediction capabilities of INFO-LSTM and ICSSA-GRU-ATT were ideal in the test. Model 1 performs very well in the prediction results of the training set and has strong data memory capabilities in data analysis. Model 2 is also able to meet the stability requirements.

articleTitle: Research on Full Link Detection Method of Power Communication Network Service Data Security
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Conventional power communication data link detection methods mainly focus on the detection of communication network intrusion characteristic data, and focus on the detection of data that has been invaded, resulting in the reduction of the security of communication network business data. Therefore, a full link detection method of power communication network service data security is designed. In the process of data transmission, exchange and sharing of power communication network, detect the security threat of power communication network service data, and describe the link threat type in the form of protocol to provide data guarantee for data link detection. Deploy the vulnerable link detection mechanism of power communication data, take the vulnerable link as the target of the data attack, predict and deploy the detection mechanism according to the attack mode of the vulnerable link, respond in time when the attack just occurs, and ensure the security of communication data. The contrast experiment verifies that the detection method is more accurate and can be applied in real life.

articleTitle: Color works ranking based on multi-scale texture enhancement and style representation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The ranking of color works is an important task to assist art education. Color works express the image through color coordination and composition, which is significantly different from other visual tasks in terms of visual characteristics, image semantics and aesthetic criteria. Currently, there is little research on the ranking of teaching color works, and the relevant color datasets is not suitable for ranking requirements. To address these issues, we first collect 4068 color works and construct a dataset. Then, we propose a novel network architecture for automatic ranking of color works. This network reuses knowledge from large datasets through transfer learning, and leverages the style and texture of images to improve the performance of CNN in color ranking. The network consists of two branches: the style representation branch and the texture feature branch. The style representation branch incorporates the importance of style information into feature maps through a style-based weight recalibration module, enhancing the style representation of features. The other branch uses a multi-scale feature texture enhancement module to extract multi-scale and global texture information in the deep features. Experimental results on the color works dataset show that our method outperforms other methods.

articleTitle: Research on Oil Well Daily Production Forecasting Model based on FWA-CNN-LSTM Hybrid Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the increasing importance of oil field production, ensuring the sustainable development of the oil industry has become increasingly urgent. In this study, an advanced oil well daily production forecasting method based on FWA-CNN-LSTM hybrid optimization model is explored. This hybrid model combines the Fireworks Algorithm (FWA), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Long Short-Term Memory Network (LSTM). By utilizing CNN for feature extraction and LSTM for modeling in artificial intelligence technology, this method significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of oil well daily production forecasting. The global optimization capability of the FWA algorithm plays a key role in accelerating the search for optimal hyperparameters in the CNN-LSTM model. Finally, through simulation experiments on the data of the Yao-xxx well in the second oil production operation area of the Changqing Oilfield, the research results show that compared to various other models, the proposed FWA-CNN-LSTM hybrid optimization model demonstrates superior accuracy in oil well daily production forecasting.

articleTitle: FastICA-based noise reduction algorithm for surface electromyographic signals
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Surface Electromyography (sEMG) signals is an important element in human-computer interaction, and significantly affect the quality of subsequent research and applications. This study introduces a noise reduction approach based on Fast Independent Component Analysis (FastICA) algorithm. Firstly, process of FastICA is outlined briefly, and its theoretical feasibility is discussed. Then, in order to estimate the noise reduction effectiveness, sEMG sinal of grasping action which is served as the signal source has been acquired by a physiological signal amplifier. Finally, FastICA algorithm is employed to obtain independent components. After analyzing Kurtosis value of each component, identified gauissian noise will be set to zero to complete the noise reduction process. The result demonstrates that the FastICA-based noise reduction algorithm can eliminate Gaussian noise components in sEMG signals.

articleTitle: Artificial intelligence pathfinding based on Unreal Engine 5 hexagonal grid map
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper proposes an A* artificial intelligence pathfinding algorithm based on the hexagonal grid map of Unreal Engine 5. This algorithm utilizes the rich tools and resources provided by Unreal Engine 5 to evaluate each node through a heuristic function, thus finding the shortest path. Test results show that this algorithm not only can quickly find the shortest path, but also can effectively avoid obstacle grids, with advantages such as high efficiency, flexibility, and scalability. This research result has high practical value for solving pathfinding problems on hexagonal grid maps and can provide strong support for game development and other fields of artificial intelligence applications.

articleTitle: Dimensionality Reduction via Geometric Modeling of Topology-Optimized Devices for Machine Learning-based Inverse Design
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Machine learning techniques have been increasingly applied in the inverse design of nanophotonics. A well-trained neural network can generate devices with diverse functions, obviating the requirement for repeated optimization processes for each type of devices. Topology optimization is a mainstream optimization strategy in inverse design, which excels in designing compact, high-performance devices, yet its high degree of freedom introduces challenges for the application of machine learning techniques. We present a novel scheme for adapting machine learning techniques into topology optimization of nanophotonic devices, breaking the convention where machine learning techniques were applied only in the design of devices with limited parameters. This scheme reduces the parameter dimension of topology-optimized devices from the order of 10<sup>3</sup> to 10<sup>1</sup> through a structure simplification process and B-spline geometric modeling, and subsequently utilizes a conditional generative network to generate devices with various functions in the new parameter space. As a demonstration, we present for the first time a set of T-junctions with continuous power splitting ratios ranging from 0 to 0.5, achieving transmissions exceeding 90% at 1550 nm across all ratios within a compact footprint of 2.8×2.8 μm<sup>2</sup>.

articleTitle: Text Feature Representation via LSTM and Manifold Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: As we all know, LSTM is a very effective text feature representation model based on deep learning, so it has excellent performance in text classification and sequence labeling problems. In this paper, we propose a novel text feature representation model based on LSTM, which creatively incorporates manifold learning methods, which can maintain the geometric structure between sentences. First, we obtain the vector representation of text based on LSTM, which contains text sequence information. Then, manifold learning method is used to construct the adjacency graph structure of text representations to characterize the local geometric structure information of text representations, thereby revealing the essential laws between texts. By introducing manifold learning methods, our model can learn the potential relationships between texts, which can help improve the performance of downstream tasks. In common natural language tasks such as text classification and named entity recognition, we designed some experiments to compare the proposed model with the conventional LSTM models. The experimental results show that the model incorporating manifold learning achieves better performance than the baseline model.

articleTitle: Research on the 5G MEC Co-construction and Sharing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper summarizes the required network extension of Multi-Access Edge Computing (MEC) docking transmission bearer scheme in the scenario of 5G network co-construction and sharing, and proposes to logically divide the integration of MEC system with different telecom operators into two levels: MEC edge network integration and MEC business system integration. Referring to the idea of MEC Federation, a new method of 5G MEC co-construction and sharing is proposed to support telecom operators implementing 5G network co-construction and sharing to share a MEC system and realize the sharing of edge computing resource.

articleTitle: LWDA-Net: A Lightweight Dual-Attention Network for Single Image Dehazing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Single image dehazing remains a challenging problem in vision tasks. In this paper, we propose an end-to-end Lightweight Dual Attention Network (LWDA-Net) for direct recovery of haze-free images.The key part of the LWDA-Net architecture is the novel Dual Attention (DA) module, which takes into account completely different weighting information between samples and provides stronger regularisation.The DA module unequally handles feature maps with different sized kernels, offering more possibilities to handle different types of information, the DA module can dynamically modify the local receptive field size of neurons, making the model more flexible to adapt to the diversity of inputs. Attention-based LWDA-Net is a neural network architecture that dynamically learns feature weights from the DA module, prioritizing important features. Notably, it retains and conveys shallow information to deeper layers. Experimental results show that our proposed LWDA-Net outperforms previous single-image dehazing methods both quantitatively and qualitatively, and even outperforms them in the dehazing task on the SOTS dataset.

articleTitle: Research on Prediction of Shield Misalignment Based on LRTC-TNN and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative predictive model, LW-LSTM, combining Low-Rank Tensor Completion with Truncated Nuclear Norm (LRTC-TNN), Wavelet Transform (WT), and Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network (LSTM) to preemptively address shield misalignment in tunnel construction. The model begins with LRTC-TNN to fill in the missing shield time series data, enhancing dataset completeness. Wavelet Transform is then applied for data denoising, improving data accuracy for predictive analysis. The model's performance is demonstrated in tunnel projects, forecasting shield misalignment effectively. Extensive experiments show that LW-LSTM outperforms in predicting shield panel and elevation deviations, highlighting its potential in facilitating proactive adjustments in construction parameters, thereby reducing misalignment risks and enhancing overall project efficiency and risk management.

articleTitle: Fast Startup Real-Time Clock Design
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper presents a real-time clock circuit based on a fast-starting crystal oscillator and a low-power crossover circuit. By connecting the matching capacitor of the oscillator to the supply voltage instead of grounding the matching capacitor of the traditional oscillator, the noise in the supply voltage is again introduced into the oscillator circuit, and the noise current is increased to improve the starting speed and stabilization speed of the crystal oscillator. The crossover circuit uses two types of crossover circuits to process the signal at high and low frequencies separately to ensure signal accuracy and reduce power consumption, compared to the traditional single crossover circuit for crossover. Experimental simulation results using the SMIC 130nm process show that the circuit can achieve startup within 153mS and stable oscillation within 430mS at room temperature and 3V supply voltage with an operating current of 0.74uA.

articleTitle: Comparison of Adaptive Filter Algorithms for Underwater Acoustic Channel Estimation and Equalization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper is focused on studying adaptive algorithms which can be applied to identification and equalization of underwater acoustic (UWA) channels, which often present non-stationary and sparse impulse response with multipath. Long-tap adaptive filters to meet the channel sparseness can cause unnecessary computation when they apply classical adaptive algorithms such as the normalized least-mean-square (NLMS) and recursive least-squares (RLS). Proportionate NLMS (PNLMS) and improved PNLMS algorithms have been investigated to deal with sparse channel identification. Dichotomous Coordinate Descent (DCD)-RLS is implemented to provide fast convergence and lower steady state on mean square deviation (MSD) in channel modeling. The numerical simulation results indicated l<inf>1</inf>-PNLMS and l<inf>0</inf>-norm IPNLMS converged faster than PNLMS in highly sparse channel and l<inf>1</inf>-norm IPNLMS showed the greatest initial convergence among NLMS and its variants. In addition, DCD-RLS presented an outstanding convergence in a wide range of channel sparsity although its tracking capacity was inferior in condition of channel varying. The equalization performance of the algorithms were evaluated by comparison on mean square error (MSE) and impulse response convolution.

articleTitle: A Graph Representation with Pre-training for Rating Quicksketch works
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The rating of quicksketch works is an important job in the daily life of art teachers, and it is a challenge to apply artificial intelligence to the automatic rating of quicksketch works. At present, there is little research on the application of computer technology to the rating of quicksketch works. Most of the existing methods still focus on the recognition of art works by hand features or depth features extracted from deep convolutional neural networks. We believe that the rating of quicksketch works can benefit from both the drawing order of works and the structural correlation of drawing objects. In this paper, we propose a novel network structure for the rating of quicksketch works. Firstly, the network learns the deep abstract features through the pre-training model ConvNext-Base. Secondly, the feature map of the abstract features is divided into multiple patches, and learns the stroke order of the quicksketch works and the structural correlation of the painting objects through the graph structure feature module and stroke feature module respectively. Finally, We used a multi-layer perceptron to get the final quicksketch rating score. Experiments show that our model outperforms multiple baseline models, both the CNN series and the Transformer series, on the dataset we built.

articleTitle: Low-Delay High-CMTI Digital Isolator Based on Set-Reset Modulation Technique Used in IGBT Drivers
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Digital isolators have been widely used in IGBT drivers to achieve electrical isolation between different systems. Due to the harsh operating environment of IGBTs, electromagnetic interference can easily cause output errors in isolators, leading to system failures. In this paper, a low-delay and high-immunity digital isolator based on set/reset modulation technique is proposed. It employs two sets of on-chip transformers to transmit set and reset signals with refreshing information. This approach ensures low delay while significantly improving the immunity of the signal transmission link against interference. The proposed digital isolator is designed based on the SMIC 0.18um BCD process. According to the simulation results, the turn-on transmission delay of the digital isolator is 5.66ns, the turn-off transmission delay is 5.79ns, the pulse width distortion is 0.13ns, and the common mode transient immunity (CMTI) reaches 200kV/us.

articleTitle: Gfl-TTS: A text-to-speech model that combines new tonal prediction and alignment
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Despite the considerable attention and successful generation of human-like speech by text-to-speech (TTS) models, there remains ample room for improvement in the naturalness of their speech output and the efficiency of speech-to-text alignment. This paper introduces Gfl-TTS, an acoustic model based on the Grad-TTS backbone network that incorporates prosody prediction and a novel alignment module. During training, this model predicts pitch contours, uniformly increases or decreases F0 information, and introduces an alignment module to enhance the prosody of generated audio. Experimental results conducted on the LJ speech dataset demonstrate that compared to Grad-TTS, this model achieves higher MOS (Mean Opinion Score) ratings. Moreover, Gfl-TTS exhibits faster inference speeds in comparison to Tacotron2 and Grad-TTS.

articleTitle: Small Sample Classification Based on Prompt Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the development of the information age and the gradual popularization of online shopping, a large amount of transaction information is generated during the transaction process of goods, and the transaction data has enormous analytical value. For the problem of e-commerce text classification, most of the current mainstream text classification methods are applicable to large-scale data samples. For the classification model in the low resource scenario, there will be overfitting problems on small samples, while in the e-commerce platform transaction process, there will be a situation where the amount of large-scale data cannot be reached. In order to fully extract the Semantic information of short text e-commerce data, a small sample e-commerce classification research based on prompt learning was proposed. Firstly, based on the pre trained language model BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer) for feature vector representation, an e-commerce text prompt template is designed based on the idea of prompt learning. The text classification task is transformed into a cloze filling task, and the predicted classification label is obtained through model training. The editing distance is calculated to obtain the final label. Comparative experiments were conducted on different sample sizes, datasets, and models, and the experimental results showed that the proposed method had better results, verifying the effectiveness of the model and having certain practical value for commodity analysis on e-commerce platforms.

articleTitle: Application of a Multi Wing Chaotic System in Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Firstly, the dynamic characteristics of Lyapunov exponent, bifurcation diagram, power spectrum and equilibrium point stability of a class of six-wing chaotic system are analyzed theoretically and simulated numerically. The results show that the system has rich dynamic characteristics. Based on the circuit simulation software Multisim14, the experimental simulation circuit is made. The circuit is simple and easy to implement, which proves the achievability of the proposed chaotic system circuit in circuit principle, and thus verifies the chaotic dynamics capability of the chaotic system. Finally, the DNA algorithm and the new system chaotic sequence are adopted to encrypt the image, and the encrypted histogram, information entropy and the correlation of adjacent pixels are analyzed. The analysis results show that the proposed chaotic system has high security performance when applied to image encryption.

articleTitle: Object Detection Based on the Fusion of Sparse LiDAR Point Cloud and Dense Stereo Pseudo Point Cloud
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: 3D object detection is critical for unmanned intelligent vehicles to perceive their environment. LiDAR and stereo cameras are commonly used sensors, but each has limitations. LiDAR provides high-precision 3D point cloud data, but sparse distant and small objects pose challenges. Stereo cameras generate dense pseudo point clouds, but lack accurate positioning. This article combines the strengths of dense stereo cameras and precise LiDAR to improve detection performance for distant and small objects. We propose two innovations: (1) a method that combines 2D object detection and threshold filtering to accurately identify small distant objects, and (2) a local Graph based Depth Correction (GDC) that introduces a mask operation to correct and fusion small and distant object areas, filter out invalid pseudo point clouds, and improve accuracy. Experimental results on the PV-RCNN network demonstrate improved detection accuracy for distant small objects, with increased performance levels across Easy, Moderate, and Hard categories for pedestrian small objects (15.88%, 16.86%, and 14.41% respectively).

articleTitle: Optimizing Inference Capabilities in Chinese NLP: A Study on Lightweight Generative Language Models for Knowledge Question Answering
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Currently, most Chinese language models, such as ChatGLM-6b and Baichuan-7b, predominantly employ the structure of GPT Decoder. These models, while powerful, are characterized by an enormous number of parameters, which may not be necessary for tasks emphasizing reasoning capabilities over extensive knowledge base. To address this, we propose the LGLM model, a leaner model with a parameter size of 1.3 billion, specifically designed for Chinese text comprehension. Despite its smaller size, the LGLM model retains robust inference capabilities akin to those of ChatGLM-6b and Baichuan-7b models, and significantly reduces resource consumption. In our experiments conducted on the c3 datasets, the LGLM model demonstrated comparable performance to larger models. To further enhance the model's performance and address the issue of language model hallucination, we introduced QA-head, a modification to the original llm-head. This addition not only improved the performance of our model but also showed promising results when applied to other models. This approach, therefore, presents a more efficient and effective solution for Chinese text comprehension tasks.

articleTitle: Method for Fault Diagnosis and Location of Television Broadcasting Based on Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Artificial intelligence has been widely used in television interviewing, editing and broadcasting; however, bitstream monitoring remains the main broadcast monitoring method. Thus, in this study, a fault diagnosis and localisation method is proposed based on computer vision. The YOLOx algorithm was used to segment television walls into images of separate monitoring points. Subsequently, OCR (Optical Character Recognition) technology was applied to recognise each monitoring node’s name to fulfil the association between names and images. An abnormal television broadcast monitoring image dataset was established using historical abnormal images of a television station. Furthermore, a deep convolutional neural network model was constructed based on the deep learning framework PyTorch to extract features of abnormal images. The model was also used to fulfil fault diagnosis and localisation. The system could also fulfil localisation and intelligently propose fault types and solutions to personnel based on associations of radio and television broadcast streams.

articleTitle: Research on Balance Relationships in Variational Data Assimilation and Its Statistical Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Defining the background error covariance matrix accurately is currently a research hotspot in variational data assimilation. The balance relationship is a highly significant physical quantity in the background error covariance matrix, as it characterizes the dynamical constraint relationships among control variables and determines how incremental information propagates in the analysis space. Hence, it is crucial for constructing dynamically coordinated analysis fields. In this paper, we analyze the three main balance coefficients that represent the geostrophic balance relationship, quasi-geostrophic balance relationship, and the relationship between the mass field and velocity field. We investigate the impact of ridge regression methods, sample size, and sampling months on the balance coefficients.
