The results show that ridge regression coefficients are an effective approach to address multicollinearity issues, although they may introduce systematic biases. Additionally, the statistical results of the balance coefficients are significantly influenced by the sample size and sampling months, which cannot be neglected.

articleTitle: A Se-ResNet50 Based Deep Learning Method for Stomach And Tract Segementation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In 2019, approximately 5 million individuals were diagnosed with gastrointestinal tract cancer globally, with about half eligible for radiation therapy. This treatment, crucial for many patients, faces challenges due to the manual segmentation process required in newer technologies like MR-Linacs. This paper propose a Se-ResNet50 Based Unet model for stomach and tract segmentation to ease the radiation therapy. The model is used architecture of UNet and a backbone network of Se-ResNet50. We train the model using the dataset from MR scan images from UW-Madison Carbone. The experiment has shown a promising result, our model achieves a Dice Coefficient score of 0.848, which outperforms other models like ResNet50, EfficientNetB0 and EfficentNetB1.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv8 Algorithm with C2f-DCNv3 and Shuffle Attention for Detection of Coal Shearer Drum Teeth
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: To address the challenges in accurate identification of coal shearer drum teeth, we propose an improved YOLOv8 algorithm for coal shearer drum teeth detection. First, we introduce the C2f-DCNv3 module into the backbone feature extraction network to address the difficulty in capturing small target features. Second, a shuffle attention (SA) mechanism is added to the neck section to help the model more effectively integrate features from different levels, enhancing the accuracy and generalization of the model. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves precision of 90.6%, recall of 86.8%, and AP@0.5 of 91.7%. Compared to YOLOv8, the detection precision, recall, and AP@0.5 are improved by 2.5%, 1.9%, and 2.0%, respectively. This indicates a significant improvement in the accuracy of detection for coal shearer drum teeth in underground mines.

articleTitle: Consistency Framework For Zero-Shot Image Captioning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Recently, Large-scale pre-trained Visual Language Models (VLMs) have shown great zero-shot capability in various downstream tasks. Nonetheless, they are not capable of generating caption given an image. To explore the adaptation to zero-shot image-captioning, recent works follow the paradigm that utilize a pre-trained Large Language Models (LLMs) as the language decoder, then using the text embedding encoded by VLMs as a substitute for image. However, when predicting on images, model usually fails to correctly comprehend visual content, leading to the wrong prediction of objects that do not actually exist in the images, i.e., object hallucination. The cause of this phenomenon is that, during the training process, the model fails to adequately receive and integrate information from the image modality. This results in the crucial image-related information being missing during training. To address the above issue, in this work, we propose our Visual Augment Decoding Network (VAD) for zero-shot image captioning. We initially use retrieval model to search the relevant image from unpaired dataset, thus visual information is introduced during the training phase. Additionally, we employ an entity-aware textual prompt, guiding the LLMs to better comprehend image content. Experimental results demonstrate competitive performance across both in-domain and cross-domain captioning in multiple datasets, validating its generalization capabilities and superiority.

articleTitle: User Side Energy Storage State Evolution Model for Abnormal Operation Scenarios in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Under the background of the dual carbon policy, user side energy storage has been widely applied. During the operation of the power system, the stability of the distribution network is directly related to the quality of energy storage on the end user side. Once a fault occurs, it not only affects production and living order, but may also cause serious accidents such as overheating and loss of control, resulting in irreversible losses. Therefore, this article proposes a user side energy storage state evolution model for abnormal operation Scenarios in distribution networks. Firstly, the disturbance events that affect the safe operation of energy storage on the user side in the distribution network were sorted out. Secondly, study the changes in the operational status of user side energy storage systems under different abnormal operating scenarios, and explore the transmission path of abnormal electrical quantities from distribution networks to user side energy storage. Furthermore, a state evolution model for user side energy storage operation under distribution network faults is established, and the safe operating boundary of the user side energy storage system under stable conditions of the distribution network system is obtained. Finally, the triggering conditions for user side energy storage failure protection and lithium battery thermal runaway were extracted through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Diagnosis using an Enhanced CBAM-based Multi-Feature Fusion CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Addressing the issue of low classification accuracy in bearing fault diagnosis, this paper proposes a Convolutional Neural Network (CMFCNN) based on the enhanced Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM). The CMFCNN focuses on crucial features, enabling a more effective extraction of spatial features from time-frequency images. Simultaneously, it integrates the feature information extracted from one-dimensional raw vibration signals and two-dimensional time-frequency images into the Softmax layer for fault classification. Experimental validation is conducted using the rolling bearing fault standard dataset from Case Western Reserve University. The results demonstrate that, in comparison with alternative methods, this approach exhibits a more pronounced diagnostic accuracy.

articleTitle: Denoising of photoplethysmograms for cuffless blood pressure estimation via Empirical Mode Decomposition based bit plane method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Photoplethesmograms (PPGs) are the human signals that harbor an abundant information about the cardiovascular system. However, it is susceptible to the background noise and the motion artifacts. In this case, the quality of the PPGs is severely degraded. As a result, the poor estimation performance will be resulted. To address this issue, this paper proposes an Empirical Mode Decomposition(EMD) based bit plane method to mitigate the noise contaminated in the PPGs. Through computer numerical simulation, as the signal quality is enhanced, our proposed method has shown superior accuracy in cuffless blood pressure estimation compared to traditional EMD and variational mode decomposition (VMD) based methods.

articleTitle: Basketball Goal Recognition Model Based on Dual Cameras
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Computer vision technology has achieved good results in many different fields. This paper applies computer vision technology to the field of basketball sports, aiming to use computers instead of manual completion of goal statistics on the court to liberate manpower. The object detection algorithm is used for basketball detection, and the detection algorithm is improved to solve the problem of small and easy occlusion of basketball targets, and attention information guidance modules between different levels are added. An end-to-end goal recognition model is proposed to realize the automatic discrimination of basketball goals. In addition, a fusion strategy of goal results from multiple cameras with different viewing angles is proposed to solve the problem of blind spot that may occur in a single viewing angle. In the experimental results, it is shown that our method achieves about 97% accuracy in the local goal verification dataset and can meet the real-time requirements (25FPS).

articleTitle: Remote Health Diagnosis of Regional Rlevator Based on MyCat and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Elevators have been widely used with the increasing number of high-rise buildings. As the core part of elevators, the health information of motors is very important for the safety of elevators. A distributed database system is proposed to solve the problems of elevator distribution and huge state information data. In order to solve the influence of LSTM parameters on the diagnosis results, particle swarm optimization (PSO) was used to optimize the LSTM parameters. In this paper, NB-IOT module is used to transmit the elevator vibration signal data collected by STM32 in different areas to the cloud platform, and then MyCat stores the data to the distributed database, and PSO-LSTM model calls the data of the database for real-time fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Research on Detection Algorithm of PCB Welding Anomaly Based on Depth Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The soldering quality of solder joints determines the reliability of the board, and the rapid detection of abnormal board soldering is a prerequisite for mass production. In order to quickly realize the accurate detection of welding anomaly, a solder joint image recognition algorithm based on deep learning is proposed. The algorithm is implemented by adaptive moment estimation combined with accelerated convolutional neural network, which can quickly classify and detect a large number of welding pictures. The experiment selected 5,000 welding image training set tests and compared with the traditional K-means clustering algorithm and Canny edge detection algorithm. The experimental results show that the three methods have similar effects in the small ball and bridge defects, but the algorithm has obvious advantages in the case of virtual welding and less tin defects. In the 1000 sets of test set experiments, the comprehensive detection rate and recall rate were 97.92% and 98.21%, respectively, which were significantly better than the traditional method. It will have a good application prospect.

articleTitle: Intelligent Control Strategy of Urban Rail Train Based on Sarsa(λ) Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper proposes a train energy-saving control strategy based on Sarsa( ) reinforcement learning algorithm for urban rail transit. The strategy aims to achieve energy-saving driving while taking into account both timeliness and comfortability when the urban rail train is in autonomous driving mode. Finally, a simulation example is given for Beijing Railway Yizhuang Line Xiaohongmen to Xiao Village Station. Experimental results show that compared with traditional dynamic programming methods, Sarsa( ) algorithm can save 3.70% energy under the premise of meeting comfortability and timeliness requirements. The simulation results prove that Sarsa( ) algorithm has better energy-saving effect.

articleTitle: Fast blind identification of a synchronous scrambler in a noisy environment
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Scrambler is a technique to randomize the data at the bit layer. In non-cooperative conditions, it's essential for the receiver to analysis the parameters of scramblers. This paper proposes an algorithm for fast reconstructing the feedback polynomial of synchronous scramblers in a noisy environment. The algorithm consists of two steps. Firstly, leveraging the properties of m-sequences, it identifies the order of the feedback polynomial from the intercepted sequence. Secondly, within the narrowed set of primitive polynomials, the feedback polynomial will be identified through a binary hypothesis testing method. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of this algorithm.

articleTitle: Bionic Covert Hydroacoustic Spread Spectrum Communication based on Improved Adaptive Filtering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Due to the presence of eavesdroppers in the ocean, the covertness and reliability of communication transmission between Underwater Acoustic Network (UWAN) nodes are further required. In this context, this paper proposes an imitation whale whistle high-order packet spread spectrum covert communication technique based on the improved fast Recursive Least Squares (FRLS) algorithm. The method takes the sperm whale whistle signal as the hidden carrier and utilizes a modulation technique combining high-order M-ary modulation and group spread spectrum (MGSS), which greatly enhances the communication rate. A fast least squares algorithm with adaptive forgetting factor (AFRLS) is proposed at the receiver side to ensure the reliability of the system while greatly reducing the computational complexity. Finally, the feasibility of the method is verified by quantitatively analyzing the imperceptibility of the communication signals using three parameters: the time domain waveform correlation coefficient (WCC), Mel-scale Cepstral Distance (MelD), and Objective Difference Grade (ODG) value.

articleTitle: SMOTE-based convolutional neural network for Alzheimer's disease image classification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This study explores the potential of a convolutional neural network (CNN) combined with the SMOTE technique for classifying magnetic resonance images (MRI) related to Alzheimer's disease. By incorporating SMOTE, we aim to address challenges associated with data imbalance. The research also presents a comparison between this approach and traditional methods, offering insights into its relative performance.

articleTitle: Multidimensional Semantic Augmented Visual Storytelling
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Visual storytelling is a multi-modal generation task of crafting a consistent narrative for a set of sequential images. The challenge of visual storytelling is that it requires the model not only to identify the specific content of individual image, but also to connect all the elements to form a consistent and complete story. Previous methods employ scene graphs constructed by external knowledge to associate various images. However, ignoring global features may cause these methods to generate incoherent content. Additionally, there is an accuracy problem in the construction of scene graphs. The incorrect relationships between objects in the scene graph can introduce noise to the model's learning process and inject an inaccurate bias term during inference. Inspired by human storytelling, we simulate human cognition and propose a Multidimensional Semantic Augmented Network, by introducing various textual semantic information to deal with the multi-modal generation task. Concretely, we first propose a Scene Semantic Extraction Module, which takes advantage of scene textual semantic information as the central theme to ensure that each sentence is coherently related to the overall narrative. Moreover, we introduce an Object-and-Action Semantic Augmented Module to enrich the details of images from the object-and-action textual semantic perspective, which further bridges the semantic gap between visual and language modalities. Finally, extensive experiments are conducted on the popular visual storytelling dataset VIST, and the results demonstrate that our proposed method achieves competitive performance on several auto-metrics.

articleTitle: LSTM-based Trend Prediction of Public Opinion on Urban Fires
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In the evolving realm of mobile technology and online self-media, understanding public opinion dynamics in urban fire incidents is crucial for effective emergency management. This study aims to analyze and forecast public opinion on urban fires, employing public opinion data from 10 urban fire incidents for a comprehensive time series analysis. This research hypothesizes that public opinion on urban fires exhibits significant temporal dynamics and utilizes the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, along with its variant, the Bi-directional LSTM (Bi-LSTM), for modeling. It evaluates their efficacy on both a relative scale and an absolute scale. The results revealed that LSTM models are found to be effective in predicting the evolution of public opinion in urban fire scenarios, especially single-layer LSTM and Bi-LSTM models with a learning rate of 0.001. The double-layer LSTM performs effectively in the incubation and diffusion stages, while singlelayer LSTM and Bi-LSTM models are more adept during the decay phase of public opinion. Given the limitations of the current datasets, future research should focus on enhancing dataset quality and diversity and refining the models' structure.

articleTitle: A Deep Neural Networks-based Significant Wave Height Inversion Method for GNSS-R Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Significant wave height (SWH), a crucial parameter in monitoring oceanic conditions, holds significant importance in the realms of wave forecasting, disaster preparedness, and risk mitigation. Compared with satellite altimetry and other technologies, the Global Navigation Satellite System-Reflectometry (GNSS-R) technology boasts distinctive advantages that set it apart. This paper has proposed a technique for extracting SWH from GNSS-R data, utilizing Deep Neural Networks (DNN). In the data preprocessing stage, model input parameters are extracted from the downloaded CYGNSS SWH data and ERA5 SWH data. After denoising and filtering the data, an appropriate spatiotemporal matching window is selected to obtain the matched CYGNSS data as the input for the model, with ERA5 data as the label. Choose DNN to handle the regression problem of SWH inversion. Finally, the SWH values inverted by the method proposed in this paper are compared and analyzed with the SWH values of ERA5 as labels. The outcomes demonstrate enhanced performance of the inversion method based on DNN, resulting in a reduced root mean square error (RMSE) and an improved correlation coefficient (CC). Specifically, the achieved RMSE falls below 0.55m, while the CC reaches 0.69. Additionally, this suggests that the presented inversion method demonstrates commendable performance.

articleTitle: FasterLite-YOLO: A lightweight cattle face detection model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: We present FasterLite, a novel method aimed at reducing the model’s parameter count and computational requirements. This approach addresses issues such as the previous model’s excessive parameter size and high computational complexity during practical deployment and coordination with edge devices. FasterLite introduces a lightweight multi-branch network structure, replacing the embedding layer and merging layer with hidden layers. Furthermore, it combines with the C2f module in YOLOv8, resulting in the C2f-FasterLite structure. After replacing the backbone structure of YOLOv8 with the FasterLite and utilizing a dataset of cow face images captured in various complex environments, we aimed to accurately evaluate the model’s utility and robustness. Compared to the YOLOv8 model, FasterLite-YOLO exhibited a 33.44% reduction in parameters, a 33.71% decrease in floating-point operations, and achieved a detection accuracy of 98.3%. In conclusion, the experimental results demonstrate that this model effectively reduces the model’s parameter count and computational requirements, making it suitable for practical edge computing scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on Internet of Vehicles Computing Resource Allocation Algorithm based on Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The Internet of Vehicles is one of the essential technologies in the field of unmanned driving in the future. As a promising technology, mobile edge computing can provide a low-latency and high-reliability computing environment for the Internet of Vehicles, alleviate the task computing pressure of a single intelligent driving vehicle, and improve the data transmission efficiency of the entire Internet of Vehicles system. In this work, we propose a novel framework to the joint access strategy and computing resource allocation algorithm based on the minimization of task computing delay, and the joint short packet length optimization and resource allocation algorithm based on the maximization of task offloading. The efficient allocation of edge computing resources is one of the key challenges to achieve this. Computing resource allocation algorithms play a central role here, requiring intelligent resource management to ensure that data transfer and processing between vehicles and between vehicles and infrastructure are both efficient and fair. Effective algorithms can optimize resource usage, reduce latency, and improve the performance of the entire system.

articleTitle: Research on dam deformation prediction based on variable weight combination model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In order to establish a dam deformation prediction model and method that is more consistent with dam deformation and achieve higher accuracy, a dam deformation prediction method based on variable weight combination model is proposed. First, four popular machine learning prediction models are selected to predict dam deformation, and LightGBM model and LSTM are obtained Then, combined with the characteristics of each model, genetic algorithm is used to assign weight coefficients to the combined model at different times, and then the predicted value of the final deformation of the dam is obtained by combining the prediction results of the two dominant models. Finally, according to the measured deformation data of a dam, an application example is analyzed. The results show that the combined forecasting model can combine the advantages of different forecasting models, and the prediction accuracy and reliability are obviously higher than that of the single forecasting model, and it has strong practicability.

articleTitle: Short-term Load Forecasting by BiLSTM Model Based on Multidimensional Time-domain Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Power load forecasting is vital in modern power systems and is crucial for the stable operation and real-time scheduling of power systems. This paper proposes an innovative power load forecasting method, which integrates signal decomposition methods (EMD, EEMD, VMD) and Shapley values feature selection, as well as a bidirectional long and short-term memory network (BiLSTM) model. First, different signal decomposition methods decompose the historical load data, and the multidimensional time-domain features are combined with the original features, which enhances the ability to capture the complex correlations in the power load data. Then, Shapley values analyzes the correlations, and the most appropriate thresholds are determined to select the best input features, improving the model’s efficiency and performance. Finally, a BiLSTM model is used for load prediction. Extensive experimental validation on public data shows that the method in this paper achieves significant performance improvement on validation and test sets compared to traditional methods and single decomposition methods. In addition, the framework in this paper also shows higher prediction accuracy compared to other state-of-the-art models.

Author Keywords: bidirectional long and short-term memory networks (BiLSTM)

articleTitle: Research on the Operational State of Information and Communication Systems Based on Multi-Source Data Aggregation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Addressing the existing challenges of decentralized management and the lack of a unified platform for comprehensive control over the operation status of power grid equipment, maintenance operations, and resource integration, this study proposes a design for an intelligent power grid maintenance and inspection information platform based on multi-data fusion. The holistic architecture of the intelligent power grid maintenance and inspection information platform is formulated, encompassing components such as the maintenance and production management system, real-time control system, and intelligent power grid maintenance and inspection management platform.To effectively integrate data from diverse sources, a forward neural network model utilizing Hermite orthogonal polynomials as stimuli is employed for the fusion of multi-source data within the power grid, enabling accurate analysis of the grid's operational state. Experimental testing is conducted using the developed intelligent power grid maintenance and inspection information platform. The results of the experiments indicate that the platform can monitor equipment status in real-time and provide functionalities such as fault prediction, effectively enhancing control over on-site equipment and maintenance operations.

articleTitle: Research on Infrared Image Simulation Method Based on Multi-auxiliary Task Style Transfer Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Unsupervised style transfer network can accomplish the task of infrared image simulation, and the core of its goal is to migrate the style of infrared images into visible images while maintaining the content of visible images. However, the existing methods have problems such as content loss, edge blurring, and poor stylization effect. In this paper, Multi-auxiliary Task Style Migration Network (MATST) is proposed. The problems of content loss and edge blurring are solved by adding coordinated attention to the generator of the generative adversarial network. The content simulation effect is further improved by adding semantic segmentation auxiliary task. Solve the problem of poor stylization effect by multi-layer style mapping auxiliary task. Enhance model robustness and generalization by domain enhancement auxiliary task. Finally, a comparison is made with other methods in terms of qualitative and quantitative indexes. It surpasses the original method in objective metrics, with 30% reduction in Style loss<sup>[1]</sup> and 5.6% reduction in LPIPS<sup>[2]</sup>. It is also more realistic in subjective visualization.

articleTitle: Brainwaves Signal Based Recognition Using Graph Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This research explores secure personal authentication technologies amid the dynamic landscape of information technology. Traditional methods face vulnerabilities such as theft and replication, leading to an increased focus on robust biometric solutions. However, even advanced biometrics carry security risks. To address these concerns, we propose a novel approach using brainwaves signal recognition technology, offering non-reproducible, non-forgeable, and tamper-resistant advantages. Our method employs Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) for feature extraction and recognition classification of brainwaves signals, reducing computational complexity. While the proposed GCN-based classification shows promise, further refinement is needed. This research contributes insights and methodologies to enhance secure personal authentication in the evolving technological landscape.

articleTitle: Investigating Population Receptive Field Properties of Optic Radiation Using fMRI and Bayesian Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This study utilized high-resolution fMRI data to characterize the population receptive field (pRF) properties of the optic radiation white matter using Bayesian modeling. Gaussian and difference-of-Gaussian models with varying receptive field numbers were compared. Model fitting showed the difference-of-Gaussian model with a single receptive field best explained the visual field topology. Model comparison accounting for accuracy and complexity confirmed the single receptive field model as optimal, suggesting the optic radiation lacks multiple subpopulation receptive fields within voxels. Overall, the advanced computational modeling provided important insights into the functional properties and lack of heterogeneity in the optic radiation, demonstrating the utility of such techniques in elucidating visual white matter pathways using fMRI.

articleTitle: Real-Time Semantic Segmentation of Aerial Images Based on Dual-Feature Attention Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: With the widespread use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), the segmentation of their aerial images has been widely applied. However, fast semantic segmentation of high-resolution UAV aerial images still faces several challenges: limited hardware processing resources and high real-time requirements of UAV platforms, the balance between model accuracy and real-time efficiency, and the poor inference ability of models for small target classes in aerial images. To address these issues, this paper proposes a lightweight remote sensing image bilateral segmentation network (RS-BiseNet) that achieves good inference accuracy and real-time performance for aerial images. Specifically, inspired by the concept of receptive fields, a deep separable fusion pyramid pooling module (DSFPPM) is proposed to rapidly extract multi-scale contextual information from different receptive fields. Furthermore, a dual feature attention module (DFAM) and a feature fusion module (FFM) are proposed based on the channel attention mechanism to extract fine-grained details. RS-BiseNet was evaluated on the ISPRS Potsdam dataset and obtained an improvement of 2.96% MIoU and 1.59% OA over Aerial-BiSeNet.

articleTitle: ConvTransSleepNet: A Novel Framework for EEG-based Automatic Sleep Staging in Wearable Sleep Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Sleep stage classification is pivotal for the accurate diagnosis of sleep disorders. Traditional methodologies, characterized by their labor-intensive nature, often fall short in precision, particularly when applied to single-channel wearable technologies. Introducing ConvTransSleepNet, a novel framework that synergizes the capabilities of convolutional neural networks with transformer layers, we mark a significant leap forward in accuracy for single-channel EEG-based sleep stage determination. Upon evaluation using the noise-reduced Fpz-Cz EEG signals from the Sleep-EDF Expanded dataset, our model demonstrated superior performance, achieving an average accuracy of 0.84 and an F1 score of 0.79 across 78 subjects, thereby surpassing competing algorithms. ConvTransSleepNet’s efficiency in rendering precise sleep stage assessments underscores its potential for integration into an array of wearable devices, facilitating broader access to advanced sleep analysis.

articleTitle: Trans-cache: a caching mechanism for LSM-tree based on filtering and transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In the field of large-scale data processing, databases built on Log-Structured Merge Trees (LSM-trees) have gained wide acceptance due to their superior write performance. However, their relative weaker read performance, especially when dealing with massive disk I/O operations and complex cache management, remains a significant drawback. Existing block cache and KV cache strategies alleviate this issue to some extent, but challenges still persist in terms of cache invalidation, memory space wastage, and inconsistent optimization effects for different queries. This study proposes and implements a novel cache structure capable of conditionally converting block cache into KV cache, thus enabling more precise caching of frequently point queried key-value pairs. This not only significantly enhances point query performance, but also reduces wastage of memory space, while mitigating cache invalidation issues caused by merge operations. Our experiments show that using the same size of memory, the new strategy resulted in a 14% performance improvement for point queries compared to the original LevelDB.

articleTitle: A high-speed CRC-32 Implementation on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) is widely used for transmission error detection in various communication interfaces. As the transmission rate increases, accelerating CRC with lower resource consumption for high-speed interfaces becomes significant. This paper analyzes and implements a typical CRC algorithm (Stride-x) and designs a padding-zero strategy to support the input data length with multiples of byte. Besides, experiments are conducted to validate the proposed algorithm on Xilinx FPGA platforms. When stride is 1, the proposed algorithm outperforms a typical parallel CRC algorithm in throughput and resource consumption with various input bus widths (32/128/256 bits).

articleTitle: DeepWS: Dynamic Workflow Scheduling in Heterogeneous Cloud Clusters with Edge-Aware Reinforcement Learning and Graph Convolution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper introduces DeepWS, a dynamic scheduling algorithm that leverages the A2C (Actor-Critic) reinforcement learning algorithm and Graph Convolution Network (GCN) techniques. Unlike existing models, DeepWS does not necessitate prior knowledge of the entire Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), enhancing scalability and enabling versatility across diverse DAG graphs. Employing reinforcement learning and GCN, DeepWS adeptly adapts task scheduling in dynamic environments. The primary focus of DeepWS is to address dynamic workflow scheduling in heterogeneous cloud computing clusters. The algorithm accounts for task dependencies, node and edge weights, as well as the computational power of host machines and router bandwidth. The optimization objective is to minimize makespan. Experimental validation conducted in a heterogeneous clustering environment, using classical datasets, demonstrates DeepWS’s superior performance compared to benchmark algorithms like HEFT (Heterogeneous Earliest Finish Time) and MCT (Minimum Completion Time). Results illustrate that DeepWS not only outperforms traditional algorithms significantly but also exhibits enhanced scalability, making it adaptable to different DAG graphs without requiring complete graph information in advance. This research offers a flexible and efficient solution for complex task scheduling challenges in cloud computing, particularly in environments characterized by scheduling uncertainties.

articleTitle: Sequential2.0: Self-supervised Speech Translation Based on FAT Model and Replaced Token Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: This paper proposes a self-supervised speech translation model based on the FAT model for knowledge distillation, which is mainly applied to bilingual business scenarios such as cross-border goods and services marketing between China and the United States. Compared with the original model, our model reduces the inference time by 16.44% and the parameter size by 12.17%, while improving the BLEU score by 12.48%. The reduced parameter size is more conducive to the deployment of the model on edge devices such as embedded systems and mobile phones. Experimental results show that using the replaced token detection algorithm is better than traditional masked language modeling, and combining the BPE algorithm and PCA algorithm for teacher model hidden state encoding helps improve translation performance. Although our model achieves better results in the Chinese-English bilingual scenario, larger models such as Whisper perform better in multilingual scenarios. Future research will focus on the knowledge distillation and optimization of large language models in multilingual scenarios, and we look forward to more participation and discussion from researchers in this field.

articleTitle: Construction vehicle tracking based on improved YOLOv7 and DeepSORT
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: We present a construction vehicle tracking algorithm designed for complex construction site environments. Combining detection and tracking, our approach incorporates an enhanced Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) into the YOLOv7 backbone network, addressing challenges in intricate construction settings and prioritizing valuable target objects. Additionally, our proposed static status detection module enhances the tracking performance of DeepSORT. Experiments on the expanded ACID and TDCV datasets show that our algorithm achieves a 96.35% map@0.5, surpassing YOLOv7. Additionally, it demonstrates superior tracking capabilities on the tracking dataset.

articleTitle: Enhancing Recommender Systems Performance using Knowledge Graph Embedding with Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Recommender systems are a crucial component in personalized information retrieval, with their performance directly impacting user experience. However, traditional recommender systems often suffer from limitations in handling complex user-item interactions. Recently, knowledge graphs have emerged as valuable resources for enhancing recommendation effectiveness by capturing and utilizing a wide range of information. In this work, we propose a novel Auto-encoder-based structure integrated with Graph Neural Networks (GNN) layers for Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE) tasks. This model effectively captures and leverages the rich information in knowledge graphs. Further, we combine this advanced GNN-based knowledge graph embedding model and a preference propagation mechanism inspired by RippleNet, to introduce a novel model, GraphRipple, aiming to enhance the recommendation performance. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of GraphRipple in improving recommendation quality.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Voltage Quality of Grid-Forming Converters by Using Improved Dead Time Compensation Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Grid-forming converters play a crucial role in providing active grid support capabilities and fault-ride-through capabilities in power systems. The conventional approaches to handle harmonic issues and compensation lag often suffer from limited accuracy. To address these limitations, a novel dead time compensation method for grid-forming converters that are utilizing pulse width modulation (PWM) technology is proposed, which integrates a quasi-resonant controller to effectively mitigate the problems associated with PWM technology. It aims to suppress harmonics and does not require additional hardware or complex algorithms, and is not limited by the modulation method or the dead time setting. The high-precision and adaptive of the proposed strategy are proved by simulation results.

articleTitle: Implementation of Image Classification Based on lightweighted Deep Residual Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Convolutional neural networks have been widely used in visual tasks such as image classification and object detection, and have achieved great success. However, convolutional neural networks typically require a large amount of computation and memory usage, which are limited in resource constrained environments such as embedded devices, thus requiring network compression. Lightweight network design is a method of network compression aimed at designing network structures with lower computational complexity. This paper introduces the deep residual network ResNet and its application in image classification. Two different residual block structures, with and without bottleneck layer, were analyzed. A lightweighted ResNet-9 model based on 9 weight layers was implemented. The model was trained on the CIFAR-10 dataset using a single cycle learning rate scheduling strategy. After training for 8 epochs, the accuracy of the validation set exceeded 90%, and the experimental results showed that the model is suitable for application in lightweight scenarios.

articleTitle: Community Detection with Deep Attention Autoencoder Based on Subspace Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Subspace clustering, known for its effectiveness in handling high-dimensional data, has attracted attention. And the autoencoder can discover hidden features within a large dataset, yet it faces challenges in utilizing attribute information for reconstruction and capturing complex spatial structural information. To tackle these issues, we propose a community detection algorithm named Deep Attention Autoencoder Based on Subspace Constraints (DAASC). First, we design an attribute topology fusion strategy to integrate attribute information into the reconstruction of the decoder. Then, we design a subspace autoencoder strategy, using the concept of subspaces to construct the loss function, to capture the spatial structural information of the data. Experiments conducted on both real-world and synthetic networks to compare DAASC with several state-of-the-art community detection algorithms demonstrate its exceptional accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: An Attack Prediction and Recognition Method for Water Treatment System Based on One-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network and Cumulative Sum
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: An attack prediction and recognition method for water treatment system based on one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) and cumulative sum (CUSUM) is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a 1D-CNN is employed as a time series predictor to establish an independent prediction model for each attack point, followed by training and learning. Subsequently, the deviation between predicted values and actual values is compared with a threshold value using CUSUM statistics to identify anomalies within the water treatment system. Experimental evaluations conducted on the Safe Water Treatment (SWaT) Test Bench demonstrate that 1D-CNN exhibits superior predictive performance compared to other models. Furthermore, CUSUM successfully detects and identifies all listed attacks based on statistical bias.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv5s fast small target detection algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of false detection and missing detection and the imbalance between detection accuracy and detection speed of small and medium targets in automatic driving, a fast small target detection algorithm YOLOv5s is proposed. Firstly, using the multi-scale feature fusion of the neck, a small target detection branch is added to the head to improve the detection ability of the model. Then the SA attention mechanism is added into the small target and minimal target detection branch to make the model pay more attention to the small target information and reduce the interference of complex background. Then, the shallow location information extracted from the trunk and the deep semantic information extracted from the neck are integrated in the SA attention mechanism to improve the accuracy of the model for small target localization and boundary regression. Finally, SIoU loss function is used to accelerate the convergence speed and improve the performance of the model. The experimental results show that the improved YOLOv5s model has a detection accuracy of 94.2% and a detection speed of 55FPS on KITTI dataset, and an de-tection accuracy of 81.1% and a detection speed of 50FPS on CCTSDB dataset, which has good detection accuracy and ensures real-time performance.

articleTitle: A Novel Polarization Multiplexing RoF-FSO System with 128QAM-OFDM Downlink Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: An improved polarization multiplexing radio over fiber free space optics (RoF-FSO) system using 128-ary quadrature amplitude modulation (128QAM)-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) modulation is proposed. The model analysis of the RoF-FSO system is carried out. The optical spectra, electrical frequency diagrams, constellation diagrams and received power versus bit error rate (BER) and error vector magnitude (EVM) of 128QAM-OFDM signal before and after transmission are tested by numerical simulation. 70Gbit/s 128QAM-OFDM signal realized transmission and receiving in 1km free space, and the BER is 10<sup>-3</sup> when received optical power is -2.5dBm after transmission. The scheme improved the transmission efficiency of the FSO system, resisting fiber dispersion, resisting channel fading, and reducing signal bandwidth.

articleTitle: Triple Attention Feature Aggregation for Few-Shot Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Few-shot semantic segmentation (FSS) tackles the task of constructing class-agnostic models that can adeptly segment novel classes with limited annotations. However, existing methods suffer from the issue of segmentation results biased towards base classes. Our paper introduces an innovative FSS method by incorporating a Triple Attention Module (TAM) and a transformer-based Feature Aggregation Module (FAM). Our objective is to adaptively enhance the representation of features relevant to novel classes in query images using TAM, mitigating the issue of segmentation results biased towards base classes. Meanwhile, we employ FAM to aggregate support-query feature pair, ultimately achieving pixel-wise semantic matching. The experimental results on the PASCAL-5<sup>i</sup> and COCO-20<sup>i</sup> datasets demonstrate that our method achieves a significant performance improvement in few-shot semantic segmentation task.

articleTitle: Joint optimization algorithm based on array optimization and pattern synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: By optimizing the weights of each element in the array to control the array pattern, the performance of radar can be improved. In this paper, we study the relationship between the position of the array antenna and the weighted value of the array antenna. Based on the given desired pattern, the position of the array antenna and the weighted value of the array are optimized to realize the pattern synthesis. Since the proposed optimization problem is a non-deterministic polynomial problem, a cyclic algorithm is proposed under non-convex constraints to optimize the coordinates and weights with the least number of array antennas in an approximate given desired pattern. Our numerical experiments shows that the proposed algorithm is universal and can control the level of the mainlobe and sidelobe of the pattern, for example, it is used in the design optimization of the phased array emission pattern of unmanned aerial vehicles.

articleTitle: DWSCNN Online Signature Verification Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Signature verification has always been a hot topic in biometrics field. Recent advancements in signature verification have been greatly influenced by deep learning technologies, particularly deep neural networks. While these advancements have notably boosted the accuracy of signature verification systems, practical implementation still faces hurdles.Our paper introduces a novel algorithm tailored for online handwritten signature verification. Our method leverages a Depth-wise Separable Convolutional Neural Network (DWSCNN) that relies on Depth-wise separable convolution for analyzing and confirming signature feature sets. In comparison to conventional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), the DWSCNN significantly reduces the number of neural network parameters while maintaining a similar level of classification performance. This reduction translates to considerably shorter processing times and lower resource requirements. On average, our algorithm achieves an impressive verification accuracy of 96.92%, outperforming mainstream online signature verification frameworks. This underscores the efficiency and efficacy of our proposed framework.

articleTitle: Research and application of UAV-based high-altitude base station in air-heaven network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: 6G uses the integrated network architecture of air and earth to achieve seamless global coverage, and space-based network is an important part of the integrated network of air and earth, and the organic combination of the three to achieve seamless coverage of the global network. Uav technology is developing rapidly, and high-altitude base stations using drones as liftoff platforms have a wide range of flexible and mobile coverage, which can be widely used in emergency communication, enhanced coverage and other scenarios. This paper first introduces the development trend and analysis of high-altitude base stations (HAPS), then puts forward the challenges of UAV-based high-altitude base stations in backflight, lift-off platform and communication capability, introduces the practical application and testing of UAV-based high-altitude base stations, and finally puts forward relevant development suggestions.

articleTitle: Visual-assisted Laser SLAM Relocalization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: In order to address the issues of initial pose estimation and "kidnapping" faced by indoor mobile robots, an innovative relocalization method is proposed. When the robot encounters challenges in initial pose estimation and "kidnapping," a relatively accurate pose is transmitted to the laser localization algorithm through a visual algorithm, achieving the relocalization of the mobile robot. To validate the feasibility and stability of the algorithm, a series of experiments are conducted in real-world scenarios, demonstrating the practicality and robustness of the proposed localization algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of the new generation Power Conditioning Unit on GEO Satellite Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: The application of PCU-NG (Power Conditioning Unit – Next Generation) on high-power satellite platforms will greatly reduce the weight and volume of power supply and distribution subsystems shorten the development cycle and increase economic benefits. This article compares the structure and composition of PCU-NG and traditional PCU, explaining the many advantages of PCU-NG in power density, performance, reliability, and other aspects. Through simulation, the transient response ability of PCU-NG and traditional PCU is compared, the influence of different solar cell array currents on bus characteristics is analysed, and PCU is verified. The adaptability of NG to electric propulsion loads is presented and the in orbit satellite flight verification results are provided, achieving the first application of PCU-NG on the GEO satellite platform.

articleTitle: Perceptually Imperceptible Backdoor Attacks Using High-Frequency Information in Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Neural Networks, Information and Communication Engineering (NNICE)
abstract: Backdoor attacks, which involve injecting malicious triggers into training data, pose a significant threat to the security of deep learning models across various domains. This paper introduces a trigger injection method that capitalises on the model's high-frequency feature learning ability. The method uses imperceptible high-frequency features to conceal the backdoor during training and accumulates high-frequency components as triggers for a covert clean-label backdoor attack in the inference phase. This approach ensures high concealment while preserving image quality and perception. It highlights the broader significance of understanding human visual systems for enhancing the reliability of deep learning models in diverse applications.
